===== M0004 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.handleStmtList(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 478-520
Documentation:

Method code:
478 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
479 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
480 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
481 |     if (node.getType() == Token.BLOCK && parent != null &&
482 |         parent.getType() == Token.TRY &&
483 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
484 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
485 |       return;
486 |     }
487 | 
488 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
489 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
490 | 
491 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
492 |     // function (unless it is called)
493 |     while (child != null && child.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
494 |       child = child.getNext();
495 |     }
496 | 
497 |     if (child != null) {
498 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
499 |     } else {
500 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node));
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     // Synthetic blocks
504 |     if (parent != null) {
505 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
506 |         case Token.DEFAULT:
507 |         case Token.CASE:
508 |         case Token.TRY:
509 |           break;
510 |         default:
511 |           if (node.getType() == Token.BLOCK && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
512 |             Node next = node.getLastChild();
513 |             if (next != null) {
514 |               createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFallThrough(next));
515 |             }
516 |           }
517 |           break;
518 |       }
519 |     }
520 |   }

Original range: 1350-1375
Documentation:
/**
     * Compare this node to node2 recursively and return the first pair
     * of nodes that differs doing a preorder depth-first traversal.
     * Package private for testing. Returns null if the nodes are equivalent.
     */
Method code:
1350 |     NodeMismatch checkTreeEqualsImpl(Node node2) {
1351 |         boolean eq = false;
1352 | 
1353 |         if (type == node2.getType() &&
1354 |             getChildCount() == node2.getChildCount() &&
1355 |             getClass() == node2.getClass()) {
1356 | 
1357 |             eq = this.isEquivalentTo(node2);
1358 |         }
1359 | 
1360 |         if (!eq) {
1361 |             return new NodeMismatch(this, node2);
1362 |         }
1363 | 
1364 |         NodeMismatch res = null;
1365 |         Node n, n2;
1366 |         for (n = first, n2 = node2.first;
1367 |              res == null && n != null;
1368 |              n = n.next, n2 = n2.next) {
1369 |             res = n.checkTreeEqualsImpl(n2);
1370 |             if (res != null) {
1371 |               return res;
1372 |             }
1373 |         }
1374 |         return res;
1375 |     }

505 |     @Override
506 |     protected final boolean flow(DiGraphNode<N, Branch> node) {
507 |       BranchedFlowState<L> state = node.getAnnotation();
508 |       List<L> outBefore = state.out;
509 |       state.out = branchedFlowThrough(node.getValue(), state.in);
510 |       Preconditions.checkState(outBefore.size() == state.out.size());
511 |       for (int i = 0; i < outBefore.size(); i++) {
512 |         if (!outBefore.get(i).equals(state.out.get(i))) {
513 |           return true;

515 |       }
516 |       return false;

===== M0035 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.transformTree(AstRoot,String,Config,ErrorReporter)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/IRFactory.java
Original range: 129-175
Documentation:

Method code:
129 |   public static Node transformTree(AstRoot node,
130 |                                    String sourceString,
131 |                                    Config config,
132 |                                    ErrorReporter errorReporter) {
133 |     IRFactory irFactory = new IRFactory(sourceString, node.getSourceName(),
134 |         config, errorReporter);
135 |     Node irNode = irFactory.transform(node);
136 |     // @license text gets appended onto the fileLevelJsDocBuilder as found,
137 |     // and stored straight into the JSDocInfo for the root node.
138 |     Node.FileLevelJsDocBuilder fileLevelJsDocBuilder =
139 |         irNode.getJsDocBuilderForNode();
140 |     // fileOverviewInfo stores the last bit of fileoverview data we saw.
141 |     // We only permit one, so throwing away extras is fair.
142 |     // The fileOverviewInfo gets passed into parseJSDocInfo so that
143 |     // it can detect when multiple @fileoverviews exist in the same file.
144 |     JSDocInfo fileOverviewInfo = null;
145 |     if (node.getComments() != null) {
146 |       for (Comment comment : node.getComments()) {
147 |         if (comment.getCommentType() == JSDOC) {
148 |           JsDocInfoParser jsDocParser =
149 |               irFactory.createJsDocInfoParser(comment.getValue(),
150 |                   comment.getLineno(), comment.getAbsolutePosition(),
151 |                   fileLevelJsDocBuilder, fileOverviewInfo);
152 |           if (jsDocParser.getFileOverviewJSDocInfo() != fileOverviewInfo) {
153 |             fileOverviewInfo = jsDocParser.getFileOverviewJSDocInfo();
154 |           } else {
155 |             JSDocInfo info = jsDocParser.retrieveAndResetParsedJSDocInfo();
156 |             if (info != null) {
157 |               irFactory.attachJsDoc(comment, info);
158 |             }
159 |           }
160 |         }
161 |       }
162 | 
163 |       // Only after we've seen all @fileoverview entries, attach the
164 |       // last one to the root node, and copy the found license strings
165 |       // to that node.
166 |       if (fileOverviewInfo != null) {
167 |         if ((irNode.getJSDocInfo() != null) &&
168 |             (irNode.getJSDocInfo().getLicense() != null)) {
169 |           fileOverviewInfo.setLicense(irNode.getJSDocInfo().getLicense());
170 |         }
171 |         irNode.setJSDocInfo(fileOverviewInfo);
172 |       }
173 |     }
174 |     return irNode;
175 |   }

===== M0041 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 352-478
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
352 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
353 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects) {
354 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
355 |     // that we know to be safe
356 |     switch (n.getType()) {
357 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
358 |       case Token.AND:
359 |       case Token.BLOCK:
360 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
361 |       case Token.HOOK:
362 |       case Token.IF:
363 |       case Token.IN:
364 |       case Token.LP:
365 |       case Token.NUMBER:
366 |       case Token.OR:
367 |       case Token.THIS:
368 |       case Token.TRUE:
369 |       case Token.FALSE:
370 |       case Token.NULL:
371 |       case Token.STRING:
372 |       case Token.SWITCH:
373 |       case Token.TRY:
374 |       case Token.EMPTY:
375 |         break;
376 | 
377 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
378 |       case Token.THROW:
379 |         return true;
380 | 
381 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
382 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
383 |       case Token.REGEXP:
384 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
385 |           return true;
386 |         }
387 |         break;
388 | 
389 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
390 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
391 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null)
392 |           return true;
393 | 
394 |         break;
395 | 
396 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
397 |         // Anonymous functions don't have side-effects, but named ones
398 |         // change the namespace. Therefore, we check if the function has
399 |         // a name. Either way, we don't need to check the children, since
400 |         // they aren't executed at declaration time.
401 |         //
402 |         return !isFunctionAnonymous(n);
403 | 
404 |       case Token.NEW:
405 |         {
406 |           if (checkForNewObjects) {
407 |             return true;
408 |           }
409 | 
410 |           // calls to constructors that have no side effects have the
411 |           // no side effect property set.
412 |           if (n.isNoSideEffectsCall()) {
413 |             break;
414 |           }
415 | 
416 |           // certain constructors are certified side effect free
417 |           Node constructor = n.getFirstChild();
418 |           if (Token.NAME == constructor.getType()) {
419 |             String className = constructor.getString();
420 |             if (CONSTRUCTORS_WITHOUT_SIDE_EFFECTS.contains(className)) {
421 |               // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
422 |               // side-effects
423 |               break;
424 |             }
425 |           } else {
426 |             // the constructor could also be an expression like
427 |             // new (useArray ? Object : Array)();
428 |           }
429 |         }
430 |         return true;
431 | 
432 |       case Token.CALL:
433 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
434 |         // side effect property set.
435 |         if (n.isNoSideEffectsCall()) {
436 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
437 |           // side-effects
438 |           break;
439 |         }
440 |         return true;
441 | 
442 |       default:
443 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType()))
444 |           break;
445 | 
446 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
447 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
448 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
449 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
450 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
451 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
452 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects) ||
453 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
454 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects)) {
455 |             return true;
456 |           }
457 | 
458 |           Node current = n.getFirstChild();
459 |           for (;
460 |                current.getType() == Token.GETPROP ||
461 |                current.getType() == Token.GETELEM;
462 |                current = current.getFirstChild()) { }
463 | 
464 |           return !(isLiteralValue(current) ||
465 |               current.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
466 |         }
467 | 
468 |         return true;
469 |     }
470 | 
471 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
472 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects)) {
473 |         return true;
474 |       }
475 |     }
476 | 
477 |     return false;
478 |   }

   * Computes the destination node of n when we want to fallthough into the

1107 |     // assigned for it) versus some other decorative node that we
1108 |     // can safely ignore.  Function names, arguments (children of LP nodes) and
1109 |     // variable declarations are ignored.
1110 |     // TODO(user): remove this short-circuiting in favor of a
1111 |     // pre order traversal of the FUNCTION, CATCH, LP and VAR nodes.
1112 |     int parentNodeType = parent.getType();
1113 |     if (parentNodeType == Token.FUNCTION ||
1114 |         parentNodeType == Token.CATCH ||
1115 |         parentNodeType == Token.LP ||
1116 |         parentNodeType == Token.VAR) {
1117 |       return false;
1118 |     }
1119 | 
1120 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();
1121 |     if (type == null) {
1122 |       type = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1123 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
1124 |       if (var != null) {
1125 |         JSType varType = var.getType();
1126 |         if (varType != null) {
1127 |           type = varType;
1128 |         }
1129 |       }
1130 |     }
1131 |     ensureTyped(t, n, type);
1132 |     return true;
1133 |   }

===== M0076 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PrepareAst.PrepareAnnotations.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PrepareAst.java
Original range: 150-226
Documentation:
/**
     *
     * In the AST that Rhino gives us, it needs to make a distinction
     * between jsdoc on the object literal node and jsdoc on the object literal
     * value. For example,
     * <pre>
     * var x = {
     *   / JSDOC /
     *   a: 'b',
     *   c: / JSDOC / 'd'
     * };
     * </pre>
     *
     * But in few narrow cases (in particular, function literals), it's
     * a lot easier for us if the doc is attached to the value.
     */
Method code:
150 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
151 |       int nType = n.getType();
152 |       switch (nType) {
153 |         case Token.NAME:
154 |         case Token.STRING:
155 |           String nString = n.getString();
156 |           if (nType == Token.NAME &&
157 |               n.getParent().getType() == Token.CALL &&
158 |               "eval".equals(nString)) {
159 |             n.putBooleanProp(Node.DIRECT_EVAL, true);
160 |           }
161 |           if (convention.isConstant(nString)) {
162 |             n.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_CONSTANT_NAME, true);
163 |           }
164 |           break;
165 | 
166 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
167 |           JSDocInfo fnInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
168 |           if (fnInfo == null) {
169 |             // Look for the info on other nodes.
170 |             if (parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
171 |               // on ASSIGNs
172 |               fnInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
173 |             } else if (parent.getType() == Token.NAME) {
174 |               // on var NAME = function() { ... };
175 |               fnInfo = parent.getParent().getJSDocInfo();
176 |             }
177 |           }
178 | 
179 |           // Compute which function parameters are optional and
180 |           // which are var_args.
181 |           Node args = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
182 |           for (Node arg = args.getFirstChild();
183 |                arg != null;
184 |                arg = arg.getNext()) {
185 |             String argName = arg.getString();
186 |             JSTypeExpression typeExpr = fnInfo == null ?
187 |                 null : fnInfo.getParameterType(argName);
188 | 
189 |             if (convention.isOptionalParameter(arg) ||
190 |                 typeExpr != null && typeExpr.isOptionalArg()) {
191 |               arg.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_OPTIONAL_PARAM, true);
192 |             }
193 |             if (convention.isVarArgsParameter(arg) ||
194 |                 typeExpr != null && typeExpr.isVarArgs()) {
195 |               arg.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_VAR_ARGS_PARAM, true);
196 |             }
197 |           }
198 |           break;
199 | 
200 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
201 |           if (n.getType() == Token.OBJECTLIT) {
202 |             for (Node key = n.getFirstChild();
203 |                  key != null; key = key.getNext().getNext()) {
204 |               Node value = key.getNext();
205 |               if (key.getJSDocInfo() != null &&
206 |                   key.getNext().getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
207 |                 value.setJSDocInfo(key.getJSDocInfo());
208 |               }
209 |             }
210 |           }
211 |           break;
212 |       }
213 | 
214 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Determine if it is possible to simply use the javadoc
215 |       // everywhere rather than use IS_DISPATCHER.
216 |       /*
217 |        * Translate dispatcher info into the property expected node.
218 |        */
219 |       if (n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isJavaDispatch()) {
220 |         if (n.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
221 |           Node fnNode = n.getLastChild();
222 |           Preconditions.checkState(fnNode.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
223 |           fnNode.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_DISPATCHER, true);
224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |     }

147 |   @Override
148 |   LiveVariableLattice flowThrough(Node node, LiveVariableLattice input) {
149 |     final BitSet gen = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
150 |     final BitSet kill = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
151 | 
152 |     // Make kills conditional if the node can end abruptly by an exception.
153 |     boolean conditional = false;
154 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> edgeList = getCfg().getOutEdges(node);
155 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> edge : edgeList) {
156 |       if (Branch.ON_EX.equals(edge.getValue())) {
157 |         conditional = true;
158 |       }

162 |     // L_in = L_out - Kill + Gen
163 |     result.liveSet.andNot(kill);
164 |     result.liveSet.or(gen);
165 |     return result;
166 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.ReferenceCollection.isWellDefined()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 243-266
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines if the variable for this reference collection is
     * "well-defined." A variable is well-defined if we can prove at
     * compile-time that it's assigned a value before it's used.
     *
     * Notice that if this function returns false, this doesn't imply that the
     * variable is used before it's assigned. It just means that we don't
     * have enough information to make a definitive judgement.
     */
Method code:
243 |     protected boolean isWellDefined() {
244 |       int size = references.size();
245 |       if (size == 0) {
246 |         return false;
247 |       }
248 | 
249 |       // If this is a declaration that does not instantiate the variable,
250 |       // it's not well-defined.
251 |       Reference init = getInitializingReference();
252 |       if (init == null) {
253 |         return false;
254 |       }
255 | 
256 |       Preconditions.checkState(references.get(0).isDeclaration());
257 |       BasicBlock initBlock = init.getBasicBlock();
258 |       for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
259 |         if (!initBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(
260 |                 references.get(i).getBasicBlock())) {
261 |           return false;
262 |         }
263 |       }
264 | 
265 |       return true;
266 |     }

     * Determines whether a set operation is a constructor or enumeration
     * declaration. The set operation may either be an assignment to a name,
     * a variable declaration, or an object literal key mapping.
     *
     * @param n The node that represents the name being set

477 |     private boolean isConstructorOrEnumDeclaration(Node n, Node parent) {

/**
   * Extracts the text found on the current line and all subsequent
   * until either an annotation, end of comment or end of file is reached.
   * Note that if this method detects an end of line as the first token, it
   * will quit immediately (indicating that there is no text where it was
   * expected).  Note that token = info.token; should be called after this
   * method is used to update the token properly in the parser.
   *

   * @param option How to handle whitespace.
   *
   * @return The extraction information.
   */
Method code:
1113 |   private ExtractionInfo extractMultilineTextualBlock(JsDocToken token,
1114 |                                                       WhitespaceOption option) {
1115 | 
1116 |     if (token == JsDocToken.EOC || token == JsDocToken.EOL ||
1117 |         token == JsDocToken.EOF) {
1118 |       return new ExtractionInfo("", token);
1119 |     }
1120 | 
1121 |     stream.update();
1122 |     int startLineno = stream.getLineno();
1123 |     int startCharno = stream.getCharno() + 1;
1124 | 
1125 |     // Read the content from the first line.
1126 |     String line = stream.getRemainingJSDocLine();
1127 | 
1128 |     if (option != WhitespaceOption.PRESERVE) {
1129 |       line = line.trim();
1130 |     }

1132 |     StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder();
1133 |     builder.append(line);
1134 | 
1135 |     state = State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION;
1136 |     token = next();
1137 | 
1138 |     boolean ignoreStar = false;
1139 | 
1140 |     do {
1141 |       switch (token) {
1142 |         case ANNOTATION:
1143 |         case EOC:
1144 |         case EOF:
1145 |           String multilineText = builder.toString();
1146 | 
1147 |           if (option != WhitespaceOption.PRESERVE) {
1148 |             multilineText = multilineText.trim();
1149 |           }
1150 | 
1151 |           int endLineno = stream.getLineno();
1152 |           int endCharno = stream.getCharno();
1153 | 
1154 |           if (multilineText.length() > 0) {
1155 |             jsdocBuilder.markText(multilineText, startLineno, startCharno,
1156 |                                   endLineno, endCharno);
1157 |           }
1158 | 
1159 |           return new ExtractionInfo(multilineText, token);
1160 | 
1161 |         case STAR:
1162 |           if (!ignoreStar) {
1163 |             if (builder.length() > 0) {
1164 |               builder.append(' ');
1165 |             }
1166 |

1176 |           }

1181 | 
1182 |         default:

1188 |           }
1189 | 
1190 |           builder.append(toString(token));
1191 | 
1192 |           line = stream.getRemainingJSDocLine();

1194 |           if (option != WhitespaceOption.PRESERVE) {
1195 |             line = trimEnd(line);
1196 |           }

   * @return true if this node marks the start of a new basic block

Method code:
160 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
161 |     if (parent != null) {
162 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
163 |         case Token.DO:
164 |         case Token.FOR:
165 |         case Token.TRY:
166 |         case Token.WHILE:
167 |         case Token.WITH:
168 |           // NOTE: TRY has up to 3 child blocks:
169 |           // TRY
170 |           //   BLOCK
171 |           //   BLOCK
172 |           //     CATCH
173 |           //   BLOCK
174 |           // Note that there is an explcit CATCH token but no explicit
175 |           // FINALLY token. For simplicity, we consider each BLOCK
176 |           // a separate basic BLOCK.
177 |           return true;
178 |         case Token.AND:
179 |         case Token.HOOK:
180 |         case Token.IF:
181 |         case Token.OR:
182 |           // The first child of a conditional is not a boundary,
183 |           // but all the rest of the children are.
184 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
185 | 
186 |       }
187 |     }
188 | 
189 |     return n.getType() == Token.CASE;
190 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.ensurePropertyDefined(Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 540-579
Documentation:
/**
   * Defines a property if the property has not been defined yet.
   */
Method code:
540 |   private void ensurePropertyDefined(Node getprop, JSType rightType) {
541 |     ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(
542 |         getJSType(getprop.getFirstChild()).restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
543 |     if (objectType != null) {
544 |       if (ensurePropertyDeclaredHelper(getprop, objectType)) {
545 |         return;
546 |       }
547 | 
548 |       String propName = getprop.getLastChild().getString();
549 |       if (!objectType.isPropertyTypeDeclared(propName)) {
550 |         // We do not want a "stray" assign to define an inferred property
551 |         // for every object of this type in the program. So we use a heuristic
552 |         // approach to determine whether to infer the propery.
553 |         //
554 |         // 1) If the property is already defined, join it with the previously
555 |         //    inferred type.
556 |         // 2) If this isn't an instance object, define it.
557 |         // 3) If the property of an object is being assigned in the constructor,
558 |         //    define it.
559 |         // 4) If this is a stub, define it.
560 |         // 5) Otherwise, do not define the type, but declare it in the registry
561 |         //    so that we can use it for missing property checks.
562 |         if (objectType.hasProperty(propName) ||
563 |             !objectType.isInstanceType()) {
564 |           if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
565 |             objectType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, rightType, false);
566 |           } else {
567 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(propName, rightType, false);
568 |           }
569 |         } else {
570 |           if (getprop.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.THIS &&
571 |               getJSType(syntacticScope.getRootNode()).isConstructor()) {
572 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(propName, rightType, false);
573 |           } else {
574 |             registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, objectType);
575 |           }
576 |         }
577 |       }
578 |     }
579 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessDefines.CollectDefines.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessDefines.java
Original range: 247-331

Method code:
247 |     public  void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
248 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
249 |       if (refInfo != null) {
250 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
251 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
252 |         String fullName = name.fullName();
253 |         switch (ref.type) {
254 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
255 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
256 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
257 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
258 |             if (valParent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN && name.isSimpleName() &&
259 |                 name.declaration == ref) {
260 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
261 |               // before it's declared
262 |               compiler.report(
263 |                   JSError.make(t, val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
264 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
265 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
266 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
267 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
268 | 
269 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
270 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
271 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
272 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
273 |             }
274 |             break;
275 |           default:
276 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
277 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
278 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
279 |               // or it's an error.
280 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
281 |               if (info != null) {
282 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
283 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
284 |               }
285 |             }
286 |             break;
287 |         }
288 |       }
289 | 
290 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
291 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
292 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
293 |         compiler.report(
294 |             JSError.make(t, n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
295 |       }
296 | 
297 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
298 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
299 |         if (n.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
300 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
301 |           n.removeChild(last);
302 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
303 |         } else {
304 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.NAME);
305 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
306 |         }
307 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
308 |       }
309 | 
310 |       if (n.getType() == Token.CALL) {
311 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
312 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
313 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
314 |           //
315 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
316 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
317 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
318 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which
319 |           // are not. But this would be overkill, expecially because
320 |           // the intended use of defines is with config_files, where
321 |           // all the defines are at the top of the bundle.
322 |           for (DefineInfo info : assignableDefines.values()) {
323 |             setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
324 |           }
325 | 
326 |           assignableDefines.clear();
327 |         }
328 |       }
329 | 
330 |       updateAssignAllowedStack(n, false);
331 |     }

54 |             n.getLastChild(), Token.BREAK, n.getFirstChild().getString());
55 |         break;
56 |

68 |         if (NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(cond) && !NodeUtil.getBooleanValue(cond)) {

70 |           // but as we know the condition will always false, we can treat them

   * {@inheritDoc}

269 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
270 |     assignmentLog = new StringBuilder();
271 | 
272 |     // Do variable reference counting.
273 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, externs, new ProcessVars(true));
274 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, new ProcessVars(false));
275 | 
276 |     // Make sure that new names don't overlap with extern names.
277 |     reservedNames.addAll(externNames);
278 | 
279 |     // Rename vars, sorted by frequency of occurrence to minimize code size.
280 |     SortedSet<Assignment> varsByFrequency =
281 |         new TreeSet<Assignment>(FREQUENCY_COMPARATOR);
282 |     varsByFrequency.addAll(assignments.values());
283 | 
284 |     // First try to reuse names from an earlier compilation.
285 |     if (prevUsedRenameMap != null) {
286 |       reusePreviouslyUsedVariableMap();
287 |     }
288 | 
289 |     // Assign names, sorted by descending frequency to minimize code size.
290 |     assignNames(varsByFrequency);
291 | 
292 |     boolean changed = false;
293 | 
294 |     // Rename the globals!
295 |     for (Node n : globalNameNodes) {
296 |       String newName = getNewGlobalName(n);
297 |       // Note: if newName is null, then oldName is an extern.
298 |       if (newName != null) {
299 |         n.setString(newName);
300 |         changed = true;
301 |       }
302 |     }
303 | 
304 |     // Rename the locals!
305 |     int count = 0;
306 |     for (Node n : localNameNodes) {
307 |       String newName = getNewLocalName(n, count);
308 |       if (newName != null) {
309 |         n.setString(newName);
310 |         changed = true;
311 |       }
312 |       count++;
313 |     }
314 | 
315 |     if (changed) {
316 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
317 |     }
318 | 
319 |     // Lastly, write the name assignments to the debug log.
320 |     compiler.addToDebugLog("JS var assignments:\n" + assignmentLog);
321 |     assignmentLog = null;
322 |   }

===== M0168 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VariableReferenceCheck.ReferenceCheckingBehavior.checkVar(NodeTraversal,Var,List<Reference>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VariableReferenceCheck.java
Original range: 101-183
Documentation:
/**
     * If the variable is declared more than once in a basic block, generate a
     * warning. Also check if a variable is used in a given scope before it is
     * declared, which suggest a likely error. Relies on the fact that
     * references is in parse-tree order.
     */
Method code:
101 |     private void checkVar(NodeTraversal t, Var v, List<Reference> references) {
102 |       blocksWithDeclarations.clear();
103 |       boolean isDeclaredInScope = false;
104 |       boolean isUnhoistedNamedFunction = false;
105 |       Reference hoistedFn = null;
106 | 
107 |       // Look for hoisted functions.
108 |       for (Reference reference : references) {
109 |         if (reference.isHoistedFunction()) {
110 |           blocksWithDeclarations.add(reference.getBasicBlock());
111 |           isDeclaredInScope = true;
112 |           hoistedFn = reference;
113 |           break;
114 |         } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(
115 |             reference.getNameNode().getParent())) {
116 |           isUnhoistedNamedFunction = true;
117 |         }
118 |       }
119 | 
120 |       for (Reference reference : references) {
121 |         if (reference == hoistedFn) {
122 |           continue;
123 |         }
124 | 
125 |         BasicBlock basicBlock = reference.getBasicBlock();
126 |         boolean isDeclaration = reference.isDeclaration();
127 | 
128 |         if (isDeclaration) {
129 |           // Look through all the declarations we've found so far, and
130 |           // check if any of them are before this block.
131 |           for (BasicBlock declaredBlock : blocksWithDeclarations) {
132 |             if (declaredBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(basicBlock)) {
133 |               compiler.report(
134 |                   JSError.make(reference.getSourceName(),
135 |                       reference.getNameNode(),
136 |                       checkLevel,
137 |                       REDECLARED_VARIABLE, v.name));
138 |               break;
139 |             }
140 |           }
141 |         }
142 | 
143 |         if (CHECK_UNHOISTED_NAMED_FUNCTIONS && isUnhoistedNamedFunction
144 |             && !isDeclaration && isDeclaredInScope) {
145 |           // Only allow an unhoisted named function to be used within the
146 |           // block it is declared.
147 |           for (BasicBlock declaredBlock : blocksWithDeclarations) {
148 |             if (!declaredBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(basicBlock)) {
149 |               compiler.report(
150 |                   JSError.make(reference.getSourceName(),
151 |                       reference.getNameNode(),
152 |                       checkLevel,
153 |                       AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_DECL, v.name));
154 |               break;
155 |             }
156 |           }
157 |         }
158 | 
159 |         if (!isDeclaration && !isDeclaredInScope) {
160 |           // Special case to deal with var goog = goog || {}
161 |           Node grandparent = reference.getGrandparent();
162 |           if (grandparent.getType() == Token.NAME
163 |               && grandparent.getString() == v.name) {
164 |             continue;
165 |           }
166 | 
167 |           // Only generate warnings if the scopes do not match in order
168 |           // to deal with possible forward declarations and recursion
169 |           if (reference.getScope() == v.scope) {
170 |             compiler.report(
171 |                 JSError.make(reference.getSourceName(),
172 |                              reference.getNameNode(),
173 |                              checkLevel,
174 |                              UNDECLARED_REFERENCE, v.name));
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 | 
178 |         if (isDeclaration) {
179 |           blocksWithDeclarations.add(basicBlock);
180 |           isDeclaredInScope = true;
181 |         }
182 |       }
183 |     }

889 |   static String identifierEscape(String s) {
890 |     // First check if escaping is needed at all -- in most cases it isn't.
891 |     if (NodeUtil.isLatin(s)) {
892 |       return s;
893 |     }
894 | 
895 |     // Now going through the string to escape non-latin characters if needed.
896 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
897 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
898 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
899 |       // Identifiers should always go to Latin1/ ASCII characters because
900 |       // different browser's rules for valid identifier characters are
901 |       // crazy.
902 |       if (c > 0x1F && c < 0x7F) {
903 |         sb.append(c);
904 |       } else {
905 |         appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
906 |       }
907 |     }
908 |     return sb.toString();
909 |   }

===== M0215 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 179-264
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
179 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
180 |       boolean conditional) {
181 | 
182 |     switch (n.getType()) {
183 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
184 |       case Token.BLOCK:
185 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
186 |         return;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.WHILE:
189 |       case Token.DO:
190 |       case Token.IF:
191 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
192 |             conditional);
193 |         return;
194 | 
195 |       case Token.FOR:
196 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
197 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
198 |               conditional);
199 |         } else {
200 |           // for(x in y) {...}
201 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
202 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
203 |           if (NodeUtil.isVar(lhs)) {
204 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
205 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
206 |           }
207 |           addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
208 |           addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
209 |           computeGenKill(rhs, gen, kill, conditional);
210 |         }
211 |         return;
212 | 
213 |       case Token.VAR:
214 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
215 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
216 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
217 |             if (!conditional) {
218 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
219 |             }
220 |           }
221 |         }
222 |         return;
223 | 
224 |       case Token.AND:
225 |       case Token.OR:
226 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
227 |         // May short circuit.
228 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
229 |         return;
230 | 
231 |       case Token.HOOK:
232 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
233 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
234 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
235 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
236 |         return;
237 | 
238 |       case Token.NAME:
239 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
240 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
241 |         } else {
242 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
243 |         }
244 |         return;
245 | 
246 |       default:
247 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isName(n.getFirstChild())) {
248 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
249 |           if (!conditional) {
250 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
251 |           }
252 |           if (!NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
253 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
254 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
255 |           }
256 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);
257 |         } else {
258 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
259 |             computeGenKill(c, gen, kill, conditional);
260 |           }
261 |         }
262 |         return;
263 |     }
264 |   }

/**
   * Traverses a function.
   */
Method code:
483 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
484 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
485 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
486 | 
487 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
488 | 
489 |     boolean anonymous = parent != null && NodeUtil.isFunctionAnonymous(n);
490 | 
491 |     if (!anonymous) {
492 |       // Named functions are parent of the containing scope.
493 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
494 |     }
495 | 
496 |     curNode = n;
497 |     pushScope(n);
498 | 
499 |     if (anonymous) {
500 |       // Anonymous function names are parent of the contained scope.
501 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
502 |     }
503 | 
504 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
505 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
506 | 
507 |     // Args
508 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
509 | 
510 |     // Body

512 |             body.getType() == Token.BLOCK);
513 |     traverseBranch(body, n);

   * TypeExpressionList := TypeExpression // a white lie

1514 |         skipEOLs();
1515 |         if (!match(JsDocToken.GT)) {
1516 |           return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.gt");
1517 |         }
1518 |

1520 |       }

Original range: 121-157

/**
   * Creates a scope with all types declared. Declares newly discovered types
   * and type properties in the type registry.
   */
Method code:
121 |   public Scope createScope(Node root, Scope parent) {
122 |     // Constructing the global scope is very different than constructing
123 |     // inner scopes, because only global scopes can contain named classes that
124 |     // show up in the type registry.
125 |     Scope newScope = null;
126 |     if (parent == null) {
127 |       // Find all the classes in the global scope.
128 |       newScope = createInitialScope(root);
129 | 
130 |       GlobalScopeBuilder scopeBuilder = new GlobalScopeBuilder(newScope);
131 |       NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, scopeBuilder);
132 |       scopeBuilder.resolveStubDeclarations();
133 | 
134 |       // Gather the properties in each function that we found in the
135 |       // global scope, if that function has a @this type that we can
136 |       // build properties on.
137 |       for (Node functionNode : scopeBuilder.nonExternFunctions) {
138 |         JSType type = functionNode.getJSType();
139 |         if (type != null && type instanceof FunctionType) {
140 |           FunctionType fnType = (FunctionType) type;
141 |           ObjectType fnThisType = fnType.getTypeOfThis();
142 |           if (!fnThisType.isUnknownType()) {
143 |             NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, functionNode.getLastChild(),
144 |                 scopeBuilder.new CollectProperties(fnThisType));
145 |           }
146 |         }
147 |       }
148 | 
149 |       codingConvention.defineDelegateProxyProperties(
150 |           typeRegistry, newScope, delegateProxyMap);
151 |     } else {
152 |       newScope = new Scope(parent, root);
153 |       (new LocalScopeBuilder(newScope)).build();
154 |     }
155 |     typeRegistry.resolveTypesInScope(newScope);
156 |     return newScope;
157 |   }

===== M0270 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseVariableDeclarations.GatherCollapses.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseVariableDeclarations.java
Original range: 349-378
Documentation:

Method code:
349 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
350 |       // Only care about var nodes
351 |       if (n.getType() != Token.VAR) return;
352 | 
353 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
354 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
355 | 
356 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
357 |       // be collapsed
358 |       if (parent.getType() == Token.IF) return;
359 | 
360 |       Node varNode = n;
361 | 
362 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
363 |       n = n.getNext();
364 | 
365 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
366 |       while (n != null && n.getType() == Token.VAR) {
367 |         nodesToCollapse.add(n);
368 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
369 | 
370 |         n = n.getNext();
371 |       }
372 | 
373 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse) {
374 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
375 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, parent));
376 |       }
377 | 
378 |     }

===== M0290 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.canInline(Reference,Reference,Reference)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 478-535
Documentation:
/**
     * @return true if the provided reference and declaration can be safely
     *         inlined according to our criteria
     */
Method code:
478 |     private boolean canInline(
479 |         Reference declaration,
480 |         Reference initialization,
481 |         Reference reference) {
482 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(declaration)
483 |           || !isValidInitialization(initialization)
484 |           || !isValidReference(reference)) {
485 |         return false;
486 |       }
487 | 
488 |       // If the value is read more than once, skip it.
489 |       // VAR declarations and EXPR_RESULT don't need the value, but other
490 |       // ASSIGN expressions parents do.
491 |       if (declaration != initialization &&
492 |           initialization.getGrandparent().getType() != Token.EXPR_RESULT) {
493 |         return false;
494 |       }
495 | 
496 |       // Be very conservative and do no cross control structures or
497 |       // scope boundaries
498 |       if (declaration.getBasicBlock() != initialization.getBasicBlock()
499 |           || declaration.getBasicBlock() != reference.getBasicBlock()) {
500 |         return false;
501 |       }
502 | 
503 |       // Do not inline into a call node. This would change
504 |       // the context in which it was being called. For example,
505 |       //   var a = b.c;
506 |       //   a();
507 |       // should not be inlined, because it calls a in the context of b
508 |       // rather than the context of the window.
509 |       //   var a = b.c;
510 |       //   f(a)
511 |       // is ok.
512 |       Node value = initialization.getAssignedValue();
513 |       Preconditions.checkState(value != null);
514 |       if (value.getType() == Token.GETPROP
515 |           && reference.getParent().getType() == Token.CALL
516 |           && reference.getParent().getFirstChild() == reference.getNameNode()) {
517 |         return false;
518 |       }
519 | 
520 |       // Bug 2388531: Don't inline subclass definitions into class defining
521 |       // calls as this confused class removing logic.
522 |       if (value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
523 |         Node callNode = reference.getParent();
524 |         if (reference.getParent().getType() == Token.CALL) {
525 |           SubclassRelationship relationship =
526 |               compiler.getCodingConvention().getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
527 |           if (relationship != null) {
528 |             return false;
529 |           }
530 |         }
531 |       }
532 | 
533 |       return canMoveAggressively(value) ||
534 |           canMoveModerately(initialization, reference);
535 |     }

401 | 
402 |       String newName;
403 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
404 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
405 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
406 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
407 |       } else {
408 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
409 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
410 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
411 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
412 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
413 |       }
414 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
415 |     }
416 | 
417 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
418 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
419 |     // follows:
420 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
421 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
422 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
423 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
424 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
425 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
426 |     //    compressible.
427 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
428 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
429 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
430 | 
431 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
432 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
433 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
434 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
435 | 
436 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
437 |       // generated names of the same length.
438 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
439 |       for (int j = i;
440 |            j < numPendingAssignments &&
441 |                generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len;
442 |            j++) {
443 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
444 |       }
445 | 
446 |       // Now, make the assignments
447 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
448 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
449 |         ++i;
450 |       }
451 |     }
452 |   }

===== M0313 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-112
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n) && !NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling != null
80 |         && nextSibling.getType() == Token.FOR
81 |         && !NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)
82 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.EMPTY) {
83 | 
84 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
85 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some Javascript parsers (such
86 |       // as the Playstation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
87 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
88 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
89 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
90 |         return;
91 |       }
92 | 
93 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
94 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
95 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
96 |       parent.removeChild(n);
97 | 
98 |       Node newInitializer;
99 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
100 |         newInitializer = n;
101 |       } else {
102 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
103 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
104 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
105 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
109 | 
110 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
111 |     }
112 |   }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
1604 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
1605 |     char LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN = 0x7f;
1606 |     int len = s.length();
1607 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
1608 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
1609 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
1610 |         return false;
1611 |       }
1612 |     }
1613 |     return true;
1614 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.moveNamedFunctions(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 377-409
Documentation:
/**
   * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
   * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
   */
Method code:
377 |   private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
378 |     Preconditions.checkState(
379 |         functionBody.getParent().getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
380 |     Node previous = null;
381 |     Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
382 |     // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
383 |     // are already in the right place.
384 |     while (current != null && NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
385 |       previous = current;
386 |       current = current.getNext();
387 |     }
388 | 
389 |     // Find any remaining declarations and move them.
390 |     Node insertAfter = previous;
391 |     while (current != null) {
392 |       // Save off the next node as the current node maybe removed.
393 |       Node next = current.getNext();
394 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
395 |         // Remove the declaration from the body.
396 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(previous);
397 |         functionBody.removeChildAfter(previous);
398 | 
399 |         // Readd the function at the top of the function body (after any
400 |         // previous declarations).
401 |         insertAfter = addToFront(functionBody, current, insertAfter);
402 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
403 |       } else {
404 |         // Update the previous only if the current node hasn't been moved.
405 |         previous = current;
406 |       }
407 |       current = next;
408 |     }
409 |   }

/**
   * Add a parameter to the param list.
   * @param builder A builder.
   * @param paramType The parameter type.
   * @param warnedAboutArgList Whether we've already warned about arg ordering
   *     issues (like if optional args appeared before required ones).
   * @param isOptional Is this an optional parameter?
   * @param isVarArgs Is this a var args parameter?
   * @return Whether a warning was emitted.
   */
Method code:
428 |   private boolean addParameter(FunctionParamBuilder builder,
429 |       JSType paramType, boolean warnedAboutArgList,
430 |       boolean isOptional, boolean isVarArgs) {
431 |     boolean emittedWarning = false;
432 |     if (isOptional) {
433 |       // Remembering that an optional parameter has been encountered
434 |       // so that if a non optional param is encountered later, an
435 |       // error can be reported.
436 |       if (!builder.addOptionalParams(paramType) && !warnedAboutArgList) {
437 |         reportWarning(VAR_ARGS_MUST_BE_LAST);
438 |         emittedWarning = true;

441 |       if (!builder.addVarArgs(paramType) && !warnedAboutArgList) {
442 |         reportWarning(VAR_ARGS_MUST_BE_LAST);
443 |         emittedWarning = true;
444 |       }
445 |     } else {
446 |       if (!builder.addRequiredParams(paramType) && !warnedAboutArgList) {
447 |         // An optional parameter was seen and this argument is not an optional
448 |         // or var arg so it is an error.
449 |         if (builder.hasVarArgs()) {

451 |         } else {
452 |           reportWarning(OPTIONAL_ARG_AT_END);
453 |         }
454 |         emittedWarning = true;
455 |       }
456 |     }
457 |     return emittedWarning;
458 |   }

/**
   * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
   * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
   * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
   * shouldTraverse).
   *
   * @param n The node to inspect.
   * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
   * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
   *     will be inserted.
   */
Method code:
311 |   private void extractForInitializer(
312 |       Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
313 | 
314 |     for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
315 |       next = c.getNext();
316 |       Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
317 |       Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
318 |       switch (c.getType()) {
319 |         case Token.LABEL:
320 |           extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
321 |           break;
322 |         case Token.FOR:
323 |           if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(c)
324 |               && c.getFirstChild().getType() != Token.EMPTY) {
325 |             Node init = c.getFirstChild();
326 |             c.replaceChild(init, new Node(Token.EMPTY));
327 | 
328 |             Node newStatement;
329 |             // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
330 |             // but are handled differently.
331 |             if (init.getType() == Token.VAR) {
332 |               newStatement = init;
333 |             } else {
334 |               newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
335 |             }
336 | 
337 |             insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
338 |             reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
339 |           }
340 |           break;
341 |       }
342 |     }
343 |   }

     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *

/**
     * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
     * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
     * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
     * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.

1116 |       }

===== M0376 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 213-288
Documentation:

Method code:
213 |   @Override
214 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
215 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
216 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
217 | 
218 |     switch (n.getType()) {
219 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
220 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
221 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
222 |           return true;
223 |         }
224 |         return false;
225 |       case Token.TRY:
226 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
227 |         return true;
228 |     }
229 | 
230 |     /*
231 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
232 |      * is.
233 |      *
234 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
235 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
236 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
237 |      *
238 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
239 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
240 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
241 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
242 |      *
243 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
244 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
245 |      */
246 |     if (parent != null) {
247 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
248 |         case Token.FOR:
249 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
250 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
251 | 
252 |         // Skip the conditions.
253 |         case Token.IF:
254 |         case Token.WHILE:
255 |         case Token.WITH:
256 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
257 |         case Token.DO:
258 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
259 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
260 |         case Token.SWITCH:
261 |         case Token.CASE:
262 |         case Token.CATCH:
263 |         case Token.LABEL:
264 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
265 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
266 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
267 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
268 |         case Token.BREAK:
269 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
270 |         case Token.VAR:
271 |         case Token.RETURN:
272 |         case Token.THROW:
273 |           return false;
274 |         case Token.TRY:
275 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
276 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
277 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
278 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
279 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
280 |            */
281 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
282 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
283 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
284 |           }
285 |       }
286 |     }
287 |     return true;
288 |   }

/**
   * Extracts the top-level block comment from the JsDoc comment, if any.
   * This method differs from the extractMultilineTextualBlock in that it
   * terminates under different conditions (it doesn't have the same
   * prechecks), it does not first read in the remaining of the current

   *

   *
   * @return The extraction information.
   */
Method code:
1216 |   private ExtractionInfo extractBlockComment(JsDocToken token) {
1217 |     StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder();
1218 | 
1219 |     boolean ignoreStar = true;
1220 | 
1221 |     do {
1222 |       switch (token) {
1223 |         case ANNOTATION:
1224 |         case EOC:
1225 |         case EOF:
1226 |           return new ExtractionInfo(builder.toString().trim(), token);
1227 |

1243 |           token = next();

1245 |

1249 |           }
1250 |

1252 |

/**
   * Creates a module graph from a list of modules in dependency order.
   */
Method code:
72 |   public JSModuleGraph(JSModule[] modulesInDepOrder) {
73 |     moduleDepths = new HashMap<JSModule, Integer>(modulesInDepOrder.length);
74 |     modulesByDepth = new ArrayList<List<JSModule>>();
75 | 
76 |     for (JSModule module : modulesInDepOrder) {
77 |       int depth = 0;
78 |       for (JSModule dep : module.getDependencies()) {
79 |         Integer depDepth = moduleDepths.get(dep);
80 |         if (depDepth == null) {
81 |           throw new ModuleDependenceException(String.format(
82 |               "Modules not in dependency order: %s preceded %s",
83 |               module.getName(), dep.getName()),
84 |               module, dep);
85 |         }
86 |         depth = Math.max(depth, depDepth + 1);
87 |       }
88 | 
89 |       moduleDepths.put(module, depth);
90 |       if (depth == modulesByDepth.size()) {
91 |         modulesByDepth.add(new ArrayList<JSModule>());
92 |       }
93 |       modulesByDepth.get(depth).add(module);
94 |     }
95 |   }

===== M0402 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 410-432
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An rvalue in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
410 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
411 |       switch (n.getType()) {
412 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
413 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
414 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
415 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
416 |         case Token.OR:
417 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
418 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
419 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
420 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
421 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
422 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
423 |         case Token.HOOK:
424 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
425 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
426 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
427 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
428 |           Node third = second.getNext();
429 |           return getValueType(third);
430 |       }
431 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
432 |     }

Documentation:
/**
   * Expect that the given variable has not been declared with a type.
   *
   * @param sourceName The name of the source file we're in.
   * @param n The node where warnings should point to.
   * @param parent The parent of {@code n}.
   * @param var The variable that we're checking.
   * @param variableName The name of the variable.
   * @param newType The type being applied to the variable. Mostly just here
   *     for the benefit of the warning.
   */
Method code:
452 |   void expectUndeclaredVariable(String sourceName, Node n, Node parent, Var var,
453 |       String variableName, JSType newType) {
454 |     boolean allowDupe = false;
455 |     if (n.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
456 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
457 |       if (info == null) {
458 |         info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
459 |       }
460 |       allowDupe =
461 |           info != null && info.getSuppressions().contains("duplicate");
462 |     }
463 | 
464 |     JSType varType = var.getType();
465 | 
466 |     // Only report duplicate declarations that have types. Other duplicates
467 |     // will be reported by the syntactic scope creator later in the
468 |     // compilation process.
469 |     if (varType != null &&
470 |         varType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) &&
471 |         newType != null &&
472 |         newType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE)) {
473 |       // If there are two typed declarations of the same variable, that
474 |       // is an error and the second declaration is ignored, except in the
475 |       // case of native types. A null input type means that the declaration
476 |       // was made in TypedScopeCreator#createInitialScope and is a
477 |       // native type.
478 |       if (var.input == null) {
479 |         n.setJSType(varType);
480 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.VAR) {
481 |           if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
482 |             n.getFirstChild().setJSType(varType);
483 |           }
484 |         } else {
485 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
486 |           parent.setJSType(varType);
487 |         }
488 |       } else {
489 |         // Always warn about duplicates if the overridden type does not
490 |         // match the original type.
491 |         //
492 |         // If the types match, suppress the warning iff there was a @suppress
493 |         // tag, or if the original declaration was a stub.
494 |         if (!(allowDupe ||
495 |               var.getParentNode().getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT) ||
496 |             !newType.equals(varType)) {
497 |           compiler.report(
498 |               JSError.make(sourceName, n, DUP_VAR_DECLARATION,
499 |                   variableName, newType.toString(), var.getInputName(),
500 |                   String.valueOf(var.nameNode.getLineno()),
501 |                   varType.toString()));
502 |         }
503 |       }
504 |     }
505 |   }

262 |   void addNumber(double x) {
263 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
264 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal.traverseBranch(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeTraversal.java
Original range: 441-478
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses a branch.
   */
Method code:
441 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
442 |   private void traverseBranch(Node n, Node parent) {
443 |     int type = n.getType();
444 |     if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
445 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);
446 |     }
447 | 
448 |     curNode = n;
449 |     if (!callback.shouldTraverse(this, n, parent)) return;
450 | 
451 |     switch (type) {
452 |       case Token.CATCH:
453 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
454 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME);
455 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
456 |         // is the code block
457 |         traverseBranch(n.getFirstChild(), n);
458 |         traverseBranch(n.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext(), n);
459 |         break;
460 | 
461 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
462 |         traverseFunction(n, parent);
463 |         break;
464 | 
465 |       default:
466 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null; ) {
467 |           // child could be replaced, in which case our child node
468 |           // would no longer point to the true next
469 |           Node next = child.getNext();
470 |           traverseBranch(child, n);
471 |           child = next;
472 |         }
473 |         break;
474 |     }
475 | 
476 |     curNode = n;
477 |     callback.visit(this, n, parent);
478 |   }

60 |     Renamer renamer;

958 |   private JSType getPropertyType(JSType objType, String propName,

312 |     public void process(Node externs, Node root) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.PrototypeObjectType.isSubtype(JSType)

360 |   @Override
361 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
362 |     if (JSType.isSubtype(this, that)) {
363 |       return true;
364 |     }
365 | 
366 |     // Union types
367 |     if (that instanceof UnionType) {
368 |       // The static {@code JSType.isSubtype} check already decomposed
369 |       // union types, so we don't need to check those again.
370 |       return false;
371 |     }
372 | 
373 |     // record types
374 |     if (that instanceof RecordType) {
375 |       return RecordType.isSubtype(this, (RecordType) that);
376 |     }
377 | 
378 |     // Interfaces
379 |     // Find all the interfaces implemented by this class and compare each one
380 |     // to the interface instance.
381 |     ObjectType thatObj = that.toObjectType();
382 |     ObjectType thatCtor = thatObj == null ? null : thatObj.getConstructor();
383 |     if (thatCtor != null && thatCtor.isInterface()) {
384 |       Iterable<ObjectType> thisInterfaces = getCtorImplementedInterfaces();
385 |       for (ObjectType thisInterface : thisInterfaces) {
386 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
387 |           return true;
388 |         }
389 |       }
390 |     }
391 | 
392 |     // other prototype based objects
393 |     if (that != null) {
394 |       if (isUnknownType() || implicitPrototypeChainIsUnknown()) {
395 |         // If unsure, say 'yes', to avoid spurious warnings.
396 |         // TODO(user): resolve the prototype chain completely in all cases,
397 |         // to avoid guessing.
398 |         return true;
399 |       }
400 |       return this.isImplicitPrototype(thatObj);
401 |     }
402 | 
403 |     return false;
404 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an anonymous function? An anonymous function is one that
   * has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of anonymous functions:
   * <pre>
   * function () {}
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> anonymous:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A FUNCTION node
   * @return Whether n is an anonymous function
   */

/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
302 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {

305 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
306 |       } else if (ret.getType() == Token.NAME) {
307 |         ret.setType(Token.STRING);
308 |       }
309 |       return ret;
310 |     }

===== M0520 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GoogleCodingConvention.isConstant(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GoogleCodingConvention.java
Original range: 59-81
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>This enforces the Google const name convention, that the first character
   * after the last $ must be an upper-case letter and all subsequent letters
   * must be upper case. The name must be at least 2 characters long.
   *
   * <p>Examples:
   * <pre>
   *      aaa          Not constant - lower-case letters in the name
   *      A            Not constant - too short
   *      goog$A       Constant - letters after the $ are upper-case.
   *      AA17         Constant - digits can appear after the first letter
   *      goog$7A      Not constant - first character after the $ must be
   *                   upper case.
   *      $A           Constant - doesn't have to be anything in front of the $
   * </pre>
   */
Method code:
59 |   @Override
60 |   public boolean isConstant(String name) {
61 |     if (name.length() <= 1) {
62 |       return false;
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // In compiled code, '$' is often a namespace delimiter. To allow inlining
66 |     // of namespaced constants, we strip off any namespaces here.
67 |     int pos = name.lastIndexOf('$');
68 |     if (pos >= 0) {
69 |       name = name.substring(pos + 1);
70 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
71 |         return false;
72 |       }
73 |     }
74 | 
75 |     if (!Character.isUpperCase(name.charAt(0))) {
76 |       return false;
77 |     }
78 | 
79 |     // hack way of checking that there aren't any lower-case letters
80 |     return name.toUpperCase().equals(name);
81 |   }

/** Re-arrange the passes in an optimal order. */
Method code:
361 |     private void optimizePasses() {
362 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
363 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same
364 |       // results.
365 |       //
366 |       // To do this, grab any passes we recognize, and move them to the end
367 |       // in an "optimal" order.
368 |       List<NamedPass> optimalPasses = Lists.newArrayList();
369 |       for (String passName : OPTIMAL_ORDER) {
370 |         for (NamedPass pass : myPasses) {
371 |           if (pass.name.equals(passName)) {
372 |             optimalPasses.add(pass);
373 |             break;
374 |           }
375 |         }
376 |       }
377 | 
378 |       myPasses.removeAll(optimalPasses);
379 |       myPasses.addAll(optimalPasses);
380 |     }
