90 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
91 |     int type = n.getType();
92 | 
93 |     if (type == Token.BLOCK) {
94 |       tryFoldBlock(t, n, parent);
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     Node left = n.getFirstChild();
99 |     if (left == null) {
100 |       return;
101 |     }
102 | 
103 |     if (type == Token.TYPEOF && NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(left)) {
104 |       String newValue = null;
105 | 
106 |       switch (left.getType()) {
107 |         case Token.STRING:
108 |           newValue = "string";
109 |           break;
110 |         case Token.NUMBER:
111 |           newValue = "number";
112 |           break;
113 |         case Token.TRUE:
114 |         case Token.FALSE:
115 |           newValue = "boolean";
116 |           break;
117 |         case Token.NULL:
118 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
119 |         case Token.ARRAYLIT:
120 |           newValue = "object";
121 |           break;
122 |         case Token.NAME:
123 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the
124 |           // keyword undefined to something other than the value undefined.
125 |           if ("undefined".equals(left.getString())) {
126 |             newValue = "undefined";
127 |           }
128 |           break;
129 |       }
130 | 
131 |       if (newValue != null) {
132 |         parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newString(newValue));
133 |         t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
134 |       }
135 | 
136 |       return;
137 |     }
138 | 
139 |     if (type == Token.NOT ||
140 |         type == Token.NEG ||
141 |         type == Token.BITNOT) {
142 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
143 | 
144 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(parent)) {
145 |           // If the value of the NOT isn't used, then just throw
146 |           // away the operator
147 |           parent.replaceChild(n, n.removeFirstChild());
148 |           t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
149 |           return;
150 |         }
151 | 
152 |         // Try to mimize NOT nodes such as !(x==y) into x!=y.
153 |         if (type == Token.NOT && tryMinimizeNot(t, n, parent)) {
154 |           return;
155 |         }
156 | 
157 |         if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(left)) {
158 |           return;
159 |         }
160 | 
161 |         switch (type) {
162 |           case Token.NOT:
163 |             int result = NodeUtil.getBooleanValue(left) ? Token.FALSE :
164 |                          Token.TRUE;
165 |             parent.replaceChild(n, new Node(result));
166 |             t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
167 |             break;
168 | 
169 |           case Token.NEG:
170 |             try {
171 |               if (left.getType() == Token.NAME) {
172 |                 if (left.getString().equals("Infinity")) {
173 |                   // "-Infinity" is valid and a literal, don't modify it.
174 |                   return;
175 |                 } else if (left.getString().equals("NaN")) {
176 |                   // "-NaN" is "NaN".
177 |                   n.removeChild(left);
178 |                   parent.replaceChild(n, left);
179 |                   t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
180 |                   return;
181 |                 }
182 |               }
183 | 
184 |               double negNum = -left.getDouble();
185 |               parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newNumber(negNum));
186 |               t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
187 |             } catch (UnsupportedOperationException ex) {
188 |               // left is not a number node, so do not replace, but warn the
189 |               // user because they can't be doing anything good
190 |               error(t, NEGATING_A_NON_NUMBER_ERROR, left);
191 |             }
192 |             break;
193 | 
194 |           case Token.BITNOT:
195 |             try {
196 |               double val = left.getDouble();
197 |               if (val >= Integer.MIN_VALUE && val <= Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
198 |                 int intVal = (int) val;
199 |                 if (intVal == val) {
200 |                   parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newNumber(~intVal));
201 |                   t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
202 |                 } else {
203 |                   error(t, FRACTIONAL_BITWISE_OPERAND, left);
204 |                 }
205 |               } else {
206 |                 error(t, BITWISE_OPERAND_OUT_OF_RANGE, left);
207 |               }
208 |             } catch (UnsupportedOperationException ex) {
209 |               // left is not a number node, so do not replace, but warn the
210 |               // user because they can't be doing anything good
211 |               error(t, NEGATING_A_NON_NUMBER_ERROR, left);
212 |             }
213 |             break;
214 |         }
215 |         return;
216 |     } else if (type == Token.NEW) {
217 |       if (Token.NAME == left.getType()) {
218 |         String className = left.getString();
219 |         if ("RegExp".equals(className)) {
220 |           tryFoldRegularExpressionConstructor(t, n, parent);
221 |         } else if (left.getNext() == null) {
222 |           if ("Array".equals(className)) {
223 |             tryFoldLiteralConstructor(
224 |                 t, n, parent, className, Token.ARRAYLIT);
225 |           } else if ("Object".equals(className)) {
226 |             tryFoldLiteralConstructor(
227 |                 t, n, parent, className, Token.OBJECTLIT);
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |       }
231 |     }
232 | 
233 |     if (type == Token.EXPR_RESULT) {
234 |       tryMinimizeCondition(t, left, n);
235 |       return;
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     if (type == Token.RETURN) {
239 |       tryReduceReturn(t, n);
240 |       return;
241 |     }

246 |     }

264 |         return;

276 |       }
277 |       return;
278 |     }

284 |     }

288 |       tryFoldWhile(t, n, parent);

308 |       return;

325 |       tryFoldGetProp(t, n, left, right, parent);
326 |       return;
327 |     }

329 |     if (type == Token.CALL) {
330 |       tryFoldStringJoin(t, n, left, right, parent);
331 |       tryFoldStringIndexOf(t, n, left, right, parent);
332 |       return;
333 |     }
334 |

336 |       tryFoldAssign(t, n, left, right);
337 |     }
338 | 
339 |     if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(left) ||
340 |         !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(right)) {

344 | 
345 |       if (type == Token.LT ||
346 |           type == Token.GT) {
347 |         tryFoldComparison(t, n, left, right, parent);
348 |       }
349 |

351 |     }
352 | 
353 |     if (type == Token.ADD) {
354 |       tryFoldAdd(t, n, left, right, parent);
355 |       return;
356 |     }
357 |     if (type == Token.SUB ||
358 |         type == Token.MUL ||
359 |         type == Token.DIV) {
360 |       tryFoldArithmetic(t, n, left, right, parent);
361 |       return;
362 |     }
363 | 
364 |     if (type == Token.LT ||
365 |         type == Token.GT ||
366 |         type == Token.LE ||
367 |         type == Token.GE ||
368 |         type == Token.EQ ||
369 |         type == Token.NE ||
370 |         type == Token.SHEQ ||
371 |         type == Token.SHNE) {
372 |       tryFoldComparison(t, n, left, right, parent);
373 |       return;
374 |     }
375 | 
376 |     if (type == Token.GETELEM) {
377 |       tryFoldGetElem(t, n, left, right, parent);
378 |       return;
379 |     }
380 | 
381 |     // other types aren't handled
382 |   }

/**
   * Parses a {@link JSDocInfo} object. This parsing method reads all tokens
   * returned by the {@link JsDocTokenStream#getJsDocToken()} method until the
   * {@link JsDocToken#EOC} is returned.
   *

Method code:
139 |   boolean parse() {
140 |     int lineno;
141 |     int charno;
142 | 
143 |     // JSTypes are represented as Rhino AST nodes, and then resolved later.
144 |     JSTypeExpression type;
145 | 
146 |     state = State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION;
147 |     JsDocToken token = next();
148 | 
149 |     ExtractionInfo blockInfo = extractBlockComment(token);
150 |     token = blockInfo.token;
151 | 
152 |     // If we have a block level comment, record it.
153 |     if (blockInfo.string.length() > 0) {
154 |       jsdocBuilder.recordBlockDescription(blockInfo.string);
155 |     }

158 |     retry: for (;;) {

162 |             state = State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE;

164 |             charno = stream.getCharno();

167 |             Annotation annotation = annotationNames.get(annotationName);

170 |                   stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
171 |             } else {
172 |               // Mark the beginning of the annotation.
173 |               jsdocBuilder.markAnnotation(annotationName, lineno, charno);
174 | 
175 |               switch (annotation) {
176 |                 case AUTHOR:
177 |                   ExtractionInfo authorInfo = extractSingleLineBlock();

994 |     private void maybeDeclareQualifiedName(NodeTraversal t, JSDocInfo info,
995 |         Node n, Node parent, Node rhsValue) {
996 |       Node ownerNode = n.getFirstChild();
997 |       String ownerName = ownerNode.getQualifiedName();
998 |       String qName = n.getQualifiedName();
999 |       String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
1000 |       Preconditions.checkArgument(qName != null && ownerName != null);
1001 | 
1002 |       // Function prototypes are special.
1003 |       // It's a common JS idiom to do:
1004 |       // F.prototype = { ... };
1005 |       // So if F does not have an explicitly declared super type,
1006 |       // allow F.prototype to be redefined arbitrarily.
1007 |       if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
1008 |         Var qVar = scope.getVar(qName);
1009 |         if (qVar != null) {
1010 |           if (!qVar.isTypeInferred()) {
1011 |             // Just ignore assigns to declared prototypes.
1012 |             return;
1013 |           }
1014 |           scope.undeclare(qVar);
1015 |         }
1016 |       }
1017 | 
1018 |       // Precedence of type information on GETPROPs:
1019 |       // 1) @type annotation / @enum annotation
1020 |       // 2) ASSIGN to FUNCTION literal
1021 |       // 3) @param/@return annotation (with no function literal)
1022 |       // 4) ASSIGN to anything else
1023 |       //
1024 |       // 1 and 3 are declarations, 4 is inferred, and 2 is a declaration iff
1025 |       // the function has not been declared before.
1026 |       //
1027 |       // FUNCTION literals are special because TypedScopeCreator is very smart
1028 |       // about getting as much type information as possible for them.
1029 | 
1030 |       // Determining type for #1 + #2 + #3
1031 |       JSType valueType = getDeclaredGetPropType(t, info, n, rhsValue);
1032 |       if (valueType == null && rhsValue != null) {
1033 |         // Determining type for #4
1034 |         valueType = rhsValue.getJSType();
1035 |       }
1036 | 
1037 |       if (valueType == null) {
1038 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT) {
1039 |           stubDeclarations.add(new StubDeclaration(
1040 |               n, t.getInput().isExtern(), ownerName));
1041 |         } else if (rhsValue != null &&
1042 |                    rhsValue.getType() == Token.TRUE) {
1043 |           // We declare these for delegate proxy method properties.
1044 |           ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1045 |           if (ownerType instanceof FunctionType) {
1046 |             JSType ownerTypeOfThis = ((FunctionType) ownerType).getTypeOfThis();
1047 |             String delegateName = codingConvention.getDelegateSuperclassName();
1048 |             JSType delegateType = delegateName == null ?
1049 |                 null : typeRegistry.getType(delegateName);
1050 |             if (delegateType != null &&
1051 |                 ownerTypeOfThis.isSubtype(delegateType)) {
1052 |               defineSlot(n, parent, typeRegistry.getNativeType(BOOLEAN_TYPE),
1053 |                          true);
1054 |             }
1055 |           }
1056 |         }
1057 | 
1058 |         return;
1059 |       }
1060 | 
1061 |       boolean inferred = true;
1062 |       if (info != null) {
1063 |         // Determining declaration for #1 + #3
1064 |         inferred = !(info.hasType() || info.hasEnumParameterType() ||
1065 |             FunctionTypeBuilder.isFunctionTypeDeclaration(info));
1066 |       }
1067 | 
1068 |       if (inferred) {
1069 |         // Determining declaration for #2
1070 |         inferred = !(rhsValue != null &&
1071 |             rhsValue.getType() == Token.FUNCTION &&
1072 |             !scope.isDeclared(qName, false));
1073 |       }
1074 | 
1075 |       if (!inferred) {
1076 |         ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1077 |         if (ownerType != null) {
1078 |           // Only declare this as an official property if it has not been
1079 |           // declared yet.
1080 |           boolean isExtern = t.getInput().isExtern();
1081 |           if ((!ownerType.hasOwnProperty(propName) ||
1082 |                ownerType.isPropertyTypeInferred(propName)) &&
1083 |               ((isExtern && !ownerType.isNativeObjectType()) ||
1084 |                !ownerType.isInstanceType())) {
1085 |             // If the property is undeclared or inferred, declare it now.
1086 |             ownerType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, valueType, isExtern);
1087 |           }
1088 |         }
1089 | 
1090 |         // If the property is already declared, the error will be
1091 |         // caught when we try to declare it in the current scope.
1092 |         defineSlot(n, parent, valueType, inferred);
1093 |       }
1094 |     }

===== M0621 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionTypeBuilder.getOrCreateConstructor()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FunctionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 512-548
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns a constructor function either by returning it from the
   * registry if it exists or creating and registering a new type. If
   * there is already a type, then warn if the existing type is
   * different than the one we are creating, though still return the
   * existing function if possible.  The primary purpose of this is
   * that registering a constructor will fail for all built-in types
   * that are initialized in {@link JSTypeRegistry}.  We a) want to
   * make sure that the type information specified in the externs file
   * matches what is in the registry and b) annotate the externs with
   * the {@link JSType} from the registry so that there are not two
   * separate JSType objects for one type.
   */
Method code:
512 |   private FunctionType getOrCreateConstructor() {
513 |     FunctionType fnType = typeRegistry.createConstructorType(
514 |         fnName, sourceNode, parametersNode, returnType);
515 |     JSType existingType = typeRegistry.getType(fnName);
516 | 
517 |     if (existingType != null) {
518 |       boolean isInstanceObject = existingType instanceof InstanceObjectType;
519 |       if (isInstanceObject || fnName.equals("Function")) {
520 |         FunctionType existingFn =
521 |             isInstanceObject ?
522 |             ((InstanceObjectType) existingType).getConstructor() :
523 |             typeRegistry.getNativeFunctionType(FUNCTION_FUNCTION_TYPE);
524 | 
525 |         if (existingFn.getSource() == null) {
526 |           existingFn.setSource(sourceNode);
527 |         }
528 | 
529 |         if (!existingFn.hasEqualCallType(fnType)) {
530 |           reportWarning(TYPE_REDEFINITION, fnName,
531 |               fnType.toString(), existingFn.toString());
532 |         }
533 | 
534 |         return existingFn;
535 |       } else {
536 |         // We fall through and return the created type, even though it will fail
537 |         // to register. We have no choice as we have to return a function. We
538 |         // issue an error elsewhere though, so the user should fix it.
539 |       }
540 |     }
541 | 
542 |     maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
543 | 
544 |     if (scope.isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
545 |       typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
546 |     }
547 |     return fnType;
548 |   }

329 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);
330 |       curNode = n;
331 |       pushScope(s);
332 | 
333 |       Node args = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
334 |       Node body = args.getNext();
335 |       traverseBranch(args, n);
336 |       traverseBranch(body, n);
337 | 
338 |       popScope();
339 |     } else {
340 |       traverseWithScope(n, s);
341 |     }
342 |   }

===== M0667 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 670-763
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
670 |   private Node computeFollowNode(Node fromNode, Node node) {
671 |     /*
672 |      * This is the case where:
673 |      *
674 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
675 |      * the script.
676 |      *
677 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
678 |      * the caller of the function.
679 |      *
680 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
681 |      * back to the caller of the function.
682 |      *
683 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
684 |      * asked to traverse.
685 |      *
686 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
687 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
688 |      */
689 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
690 |     if (parent == null || parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION || node == root) {
691 |       return null;
692 |     }
693 | 
694 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
695 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
696 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
697 |       case Token.IF:
698 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent);
699 |       case Token.CASE:
700 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
701 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
702 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
703 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
704 |           if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.CASE) {
705 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
706 |           } else if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.DEFAULT) {
707 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
708 |           } else {
709 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
710 |           }
711 |         } else {
712 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent);
713 |         }
714 |         break;
715 |       case Token.FOR:
716 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
717 |           return parent;
718 |         } else {
719 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
720 |         }
721 |       case Token.WHILE:
722 |       case Token.DO:
723 |         return parent;
724 |       case Token.TRY:
725 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
726 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
727 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
728 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
729 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
730 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent);
731 |           }
732 |         // CATCH block.
733 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
734 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
735 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
736 |           } else {
737 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent);
738 |           }
739 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
740 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
741 |           for (Node finallyNode : finallyMap.get(parent)) {
742 |             createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
743 |           }
744 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent);
745 |         }
746 |     }
747 | 
748 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
749 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
750 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
751 | 
752 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
753 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
754 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
755 |     }
756 | 
757 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
758 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
759 |     } else {
760 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transfered up the AST.
761 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent);
762 |     }
763 |   }

   * Counts the given node in the typed statistics.
   * @param n a node that should be typed

785 |   private void doPercentTypedAccounting(NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
786 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();

788 |       nullCount++;

803 |     }

/**
     * Defines variable(s) or modifies types based on the content of the node
     * {@code n}. A variable definition creates variables in the current scope,
     * a function definition creates a binding, and an assignment updates the
     * type of the namespaces on which the definition is made (e.g.
     * {@code goog.FOO = 6}).
     * @param n a {@link Token#VAR}, {@link Token#FUNCTION} or
     *     {@link Token#ASSIGN} node
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     */
Method code:
333 |     void define(Node n, Node parent) {
334 |       Preconditions.checkState(sourceName != null);
335 | 
336 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
337 |       switch (n.getType()) {
338 |         case Token.CATCH:
339 |           Node catchName = n.getFirstChild();
340 |           defineSlot(catchName, n, null);
341 |           break;
342 | 
343 |         case Token.VAR:
344 |           if (n.getChildCount() > 1) {
345 |             if (info != null) {
346 |               // multiple children
347 |               compiler.report(JSError.make(sourceName, n, MULTIPLE_VAR_DEF));
348 |             }
349 |             for (Node name : n.children()) {
350 |               defineName(name, n, parent, name.getJSDocInfo());
351 |             }
352 |           } else {
353 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
354 |             defineName(name, n, parent,
355 |                 (info != null) ? info : name.getJSDocInfo());
356 |           }
357 |           break;
358 | 
359 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
360 |           int parentType = parent.getType();
361 |           Preconditions.checkState(
362 |               (scope.isLocal() || parentType != Token.ASSIGN) &&
363 |               parentType != Token.NAME,
364 |               "function defined as standalone function when it is being " +
365 |               "assigned");
366 |           String functionName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
367 |           FunctionType functionType = getFunctionType(functionName, n, info,
368 |               null);
369 |           if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
370 |             defineSlot(n.getFirstChild(), n, functionType);
371 |           }
372 |           break;
373 | 
374 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
375 |           // TODO(nicksantos): We should support direct assignment to a
376 |           // prototype, as in:
377 |           // Foo.prototype = {
378 |           //   a: function() { ... },
379 |           //   b: function() { ... }
380 |           // };
381 |           // Right now (6/23/08), we understand most of this syntax, but we
382 |           // don't tie the "a" and "b" methods to the context of Foo.
383 | 
384 |           Node rvalue = n.getLastChild();
385 |           Node lvalue = n.getFirstChild();
386 |           info = (info != null) ? info : rvalue.getJSDocInfo();
387 |           if (rvalue.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
388 |               info != null && info.isConstructor()) {
389 |             getFunctionType(lvalue.getQualifiedName(), rvalue, info,
390 |                 lvalue);
391 |           } else if (info != null && info.hasEnumParameterType()) {
392 |             lvalue.setJSType(
393 |                 getEnumType(lvalue.getQualifiedName(), n, rvalue,
394 |                     info.getEnumParameterType().evaluate(scope)));
395 |           }

397 | 
398 |         default:
399 |           throw new IllegalStateException(Integer.toString(n.getType()));
400 |       }
401 |     }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 669-707
Documentation:
/**
     * Updates our respresentation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
669 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
670 |         String name) {
671 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
672 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
673 |       // assignments.
674 | 
675 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
676 |       String prefix;
677 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
678 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
679 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
680 |       } else {
681 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
682 |         if (i == -1) {
683 |           return false;
684 |         }
685 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
686 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
687 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
688 |         while (i >= 0) {
689 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
690 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
691 |         }
692 |       }
693 | 
694 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
695 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
696 |         // key, so we're done.
697 |         return true;
698 |       }
699 | 
700 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
701 |         parent = n;
702 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
703 |       }
704 | 
705 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
706 |       return true;
707 |     }

===== M0711 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 261-289
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
261 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
262 |     initialize();
263 |     int step = 0;
264 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
265 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
266 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
267 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
268 |       }
269 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
270 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
271 |       joinInputs(curNode);
272 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
273 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
274 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
275 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
276 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
277 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
278 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
279 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
280 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
281 |           }
282 |         }
283 |       }
284 |       step++;
285 |     }
286 |     if (isForward()) {
287 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
288 |     }
289 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.tryRemoveAssignment(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,FlowState<LiveVariableLattice>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DeadAssignmentsElimination.java
Original range: 148-235
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if any local variables are dead after the instruction {@code n}
   * and are assigned within the subtree of {@code n}. Removes those assignments
   * if there are any.
   *
   * @param n Target instruction.
   * @param exprRoot The CFG node where the liveness information in state is
   *     still correct.
   * @param state The liveness information at {@code n}.
   */
Method code:
148 |   private void tryRemoveAssignment(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node exprRoot,
149 |       FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state) {
150 | 
151 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
152 |     
153 |     if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) ||
154 |         n.getType() == Token.INC || n.getType() == Token.DEC) {
155 | 
156 |       Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
157 |       Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
158 |       
159 |       // Recurse first. Example: dead_x = dead_y = 1; We try to clean up dead_y
160 |       // first.
161 |       if (rhs != null) {
162 |         tryRemoveAssignment(t, rhs, exprRoot, state);
163 |         rhs = lhs.getNext();
164 |       }
165 | 
166 |       Scope scope = t.getScope();
167 |       if (!NodeUtil.isName(lhs)) {
168 |         return; // Not a local variable assignment.
169 |       }
170 |       String name = lhs.getString();
171 |       if (!scope.isDeclared(name, false)) {
172 |         return;
173 |       }
174 |       Var var = scope.getVar(name);
175 |       if (liveness.getEscapedLocals().contains(var)) {
176 |         return; // Local variable that might be escaped due to closures.
177 |       }
178 |       if (state.getOut().isLive(var)) {
179 |         return; // Variable not dead.
180 |       }
181 |       if (state.getIn().isLive(var) &&
182 |           isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(n, exprRoot, var.name)) {
183 |         // The variable is killed here but it is also live before it.
184 |         // This is possible if we have say:
185 |         //    if (X = a && a = C) {..} ; .......; a = S;
186 |         // In this case we are safe to remove "a = C" because it is dead.
187 |         // However if we have:
188 |         //    if (a = C && X = a) {..} ; .......; a = S;
189 |         // removing "a = C" is NOT correct, although the live set at the node
190 |         // is exactly the same.
191 |         // TODO(user): We need more fine grain CFA or we need to keep track
192 |         // of GEN sets when we recurse here.
193 |         return;
194 |       }
195 |       
196 |       if (NodeUtil.isAssign(n)) {
197 |         n.removeChild(rhs);
198 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, rhs);
199 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
200 |         n.removeChild(rhs);
201 |         n.removeChild(lhs);
202 |         Node op = new Node(NodeUtil.getOpFromAssignmentOp(n), lhs, rhs);
203 |         parent.replaceChild(n, op);
204 |       } else if (n.getType() == Token.INC || n.getType() == Token.DEC) {        
205 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(parent)) {
206 |           parent.replaceChild(n, new Node(Token.VOID, Node.newNumber(0)));
207 |         } else if(n.getType() == Token.COMMA && n != parent.getLastChild()) {
208 |           parent.removeChild(n);
209 |         } else if (parent.getType() == Token.FOR && !NodeUtil.isForIn(parent) &&
210 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n) {
211 |           parent.replaceChild(n, new Node(Token.EMPTY));
212 |         } else {
213 |           // Cannot replace x = a++ with x = a because that's not valid
214 |           // when a is not a number.
215 |           return;
216 |         }
217 |       } else {
218 |         // Not reachable.
219 |         Preconditions.checkState(false, "Unknown statement");
220 |       }
221 |       
222 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
223 |       return;
224 | 
225 |     } else {
226 |       for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null;) {
227 |         Node next = c.getNext();
228 |         if (!ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(c)) {
229 |           tryRemoveAssignment(t, c, exprRoot, state);
230 |         }
231 |         c = next;
232 |       }
233 |       return;
234 |     }
235 |   }

   * @param chars The list of characters that are legal

131 |     @Override
132 |     public int color() {
133 |       graph.clearNodeAnnotations();
134 |       List<GraphNode<N, E>> worklist = graph.getNodes();
135 | 
136 |       // Sort nodes by degree.
137 |       Collections.sort(worklist, new Comparator<GraphNode<N, E>>() {
138 |         @Override
139 |         public int compare(GraphNode<N, E> o1, GraphNode<N, E> o2) {
140 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
141 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
142 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
143 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
144 |         }
145 |       });
146 |       worklist = Lists.newLinkedList(worklist);
147 | 
148 |       // Idea: From the highest to lowest degree, assign any uncolored node with
149 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.
150 |       int count = 0;
151 |       do {
152 |         Color color = new Color(count);
153 |         SubGraph<N, E> subgraph = graph.newSubGraph();
154 |         for (Iterator<GraphNode<N, E>> i = worklist.iterator(); i.hasNext();) {
155 |           GraphNode<N, E> node = i.next();
156 |           if (subgraph.isIndependentOf(node.getValue())) {
157 |             subgraph.addNode(node.getValue());
158 |             node.setAnnotation(color);
159 |             i.remove();
160 |           }
161 |         }
162 |         count++;
163 |       } while (!worklist.isEmpty());
164 |       @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
165 |       N[] map = (N[]) new Object[count];
166 |       colorToNodeMap = map;
167 |       return count;
168 |     }

===== M0777 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 114-170
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
114 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
115 |     switch (n.getType()) {
116 |       case Token.VAR:
117 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
118 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
119 |              child != null;) {
120 |           Node next = child.getNext();
121 |           Preconditions.checkState(child.getType() == Token.NAME);
122 | 
123 |           String name = child.getString();
124 |           declareVar(name, child, n, parent, null, n);
125 |           child = next;
126 |         }
127 |         return;
128 | 
129 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
130 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionAnonymous(n)) {
131 |           return;
132 |         }
133 | 
134 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
135 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
136 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
137 |           return;
138 |         }
139 |         declareVar(fnName, n.getFirstChild(), n, parent, null, n);
140 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
141 | 
142 |       case Token.CATCH:
143 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
144 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME);
145 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
146 |         // is the code block
147 | 
148 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
149 |         final Node block = var.getNext().getNext();
150 | 
151 |         declareVar(var.getString(), var, n, parent, null, n);
152 |         scanVars(block, n);
153 |         return;  // only one child to scan
154 | 
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |         sourceName = (String) n.getProp(Node.SOURCENAME_PROP);
157 |         break;
158 |     }
159 | 
160 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
161 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
162 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
163 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
164 |            child != null;) {
165 |         Node next = child.getNext();
166 |         scanVars(child, n);
167 |         child = next;
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

Method code:
126 |   @Override
127 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
128 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !NodeUtil.isName(n) ||
129 |         NodeUtil.isFunction(parent)) {
130 |       // Don't rename named functions.
131 |       return;
132 |     }
133 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
134 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
135 |     if (vNode == null) {
136 |       // This is not a local.
137 |       return;
138 |     }
139 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
140 |     
141 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
142 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
143 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
144 |         return;
145 |       }
146 | 
147 |       // Rename.
148 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
149 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
150 | 
151 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
152 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
153 |       }
154 |     } else {
155 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
156 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
157 |       // make this fast.
158 |       String pseudoName = null;
159 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
160 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
161 |         Var iVar = i.next();
162 |         
163 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
164 |         // and it is merged with the current coalscedVar.
165 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
166 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
167 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
168 |         }
169 |       }
170 |       
171 |       // Keep its original name.
172 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
173 |         return;
174 |       }
175 |       
176 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
177 |       
178 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
179 |         pseudoName += "$";
180 |       }
181 |       
182 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
183 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
184 | 
185 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
186 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
187 |       }
188 |     }
189 |   }

===== M0809 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VarCheck.java
Original range: 89-170
Documentation:
/** {@inheritDoc} */
Method code:
89 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
90 |     if (n.getType() != Token.NAME) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 | 
94 |     if (NodeUtil.isLabelName(n)) {
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     String varName = n.getString();
99 | 
100 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
101 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
102 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunction(parent));
103 | 
104 |       // A function declaration with an empty name passes Rhino,
105 |       // but is supposed to be a syntax error according to the spec.
106 |       if (!NodeUtil.isAnonymousFunction(parent)) {
107 |         t.report(n, INVALID_FUNCTION_DECL);
108 |       }
109 |       return;
110 |     }
111 | 
112 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
113 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
114 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
115 |     if (var == null) {
116 |       if (NodeUtil.isAnonymousFunction(parent)) {
117 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
118 |         // current scope.
119 |       } else {
120 |         t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
121 | 
122 |         if (sanityCheck) {
123 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
124 |         } else {
125 |           // Create a new variable in a synthetic script. This will prevent
126 |           // subsequent compiler passes from crashing.
127 |           Node nameNode = Node.newString(Token.NAME, varName);
128 |           getSynthesizedExternsRoot().addChildToBack(
129 |               new Node(Token.VAR, nameNode));
130 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, nameNode,
131 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
132 |         }
133 |       }
134 |       return;
135 |     }
136 | 
137 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
138 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
139 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
140 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
141 |       return;
142 |     }
143 | 
144 |     // Check module dependencies.
145 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
146 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
147 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
148 |     if (varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
149 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
150 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
151 |       } else {
152 |         if (!sanityCheck && scope.isGlobal()) {
153 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
154 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
155 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
156 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
157 |           } else {
158 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
159 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
160 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
161 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
162 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
163 |           }
164 |         } else {
165 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
166 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
167 |         }
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

===== M0831 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.consume(List<PassFactory>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 113-134
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
113 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
114 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
115 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
116 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
117 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
118 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
119 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
120 | 
121 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
122 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
123 |         }
124 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
125 |       } else {
126 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
127 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
128 |       }
129 |     }
130 | 
131 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
132 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
133 |     }
134 |   }

Method code:
232 |   void addOp(String op, boolean binOp) {
233 |     maybeEndStatement();
234 | 
235 |     char first = op.charAt(0);
236 |     char prev = getLastChar();
237 | 
238 |     if ((first == '+' || first == '-') && prev == first) {
239 |       // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of
240 |       // things like "x + ++y" or "x++ + ++y"
241 |       append(" ");
242 |     } else if (Character.isLetter(first) &&
243 |                isWordChar(prev)) {

245 |       append(" ");
246 |     } else if (prev == '-' && first == '>') {
247 |       // Make sure that we don't emit -->
248 |       append(" ");
249 |     }
250 | 
251 |     // Allow formating around the operator.
252 |     appendOp(op, binOp);
253 |

255 |     // operator on the other hand is not. We only line break after a bin op

258 |       maybeCutLine();

===== M0903 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckSideEffects.java
Original range: 49-120
Documentation:

Method code:
49 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
50 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
51 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
52 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
53 |     // so we'll allow it.
54 |     if (n.getType() == Token.EMPTY ||
55 |         n.getType() == Token.COMMA) {
56 |       return;
57 |     }
58 | 
59 |     if (parent == null)
60 |       return;
61 | 
62 |     int pt = parent.getType();
63 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
64 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
65 |       if (gramps.getType() == Token.CALL &&
66 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
67 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
68 |         // call to an eval. See Ecma-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's ok for the first
69 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
70 |         // an eval.
71 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
72 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
73 |             n.getNext().getType() == Token.NAME &&
74 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
75 |           return;
76 |         }
77 |       }
78 | 
79 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
80 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
81 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
82 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
83 |             continue;
84 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
85 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
86 |             return;
87 |           else
88 |             break;
89 |         }
90 |       }
91 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
92 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
93 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
94 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
95 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
96 |         // of a for.
97 |       } else {
98 |         return;  // it might be ok to not have a side-effect
99 |       }
100 |     }
101 |     if (NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType()) ||

/**
     * Determines whether the reference collection describes a variable that
     * is initialized to an immutable value, never modified, and defined before
     * every reference.
     */
Method code:
624 |     private boolean isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var v,
625 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
626 |       List<Reference> refSet = refInfo.references;
627 |       int startingReadRef = 1;
628 |       Reference refDecl = refSet.get(0);
629 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(refDecl)) {
630 |         return false;
631 |       }
632 | 
633 |       boolean isNeverAssigned = refInfo.isNeverAssigned();
634 |       // For values that are never assigned, only the references need to be
635 |       // checked.
636 |       if (!isNeverAssigned) {
637 |         Reference refInit = refInfo.getInitializingReference();
638 |         if (!isValidInitialization(refInit)) {
639 |           return false;

643 |           Preconditions.checkState(refInit == refSet.get(1));
644 |           startingReadRef = 2;
645 |         }
646 | 
647 |         if (!refInfo.isWellDefined()) {
648 |           return false;
649 |         }
650 |

652 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
653 |         if (!(NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value) &&
654 |             (value.getType() != Token.STRING ||
655 |              isStringWorthInlining(v, refInfo.references)))) {
656 |           return false;
657 |         }
658 | 
659 |       }
660 | 
661 |       for (int i = startingReadRef; i < refSet.size(); i++) {
662 |         Reference ref = refSet.get(i);
663 |         if (!isValidReference(ref)) {
664 |           return false;
665 |         }
666 |       }
667 |

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.updateScopeForTypeChange(FlowScope,Node,JSType,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 489-535
Documentation:
/**
   * Updates the scope according to the result of a type change, like
   * an assignment or a type cast.
   */
Method code:
489 |   private void updateScopeForTypeChange(
490 |       FlowScope scope, Node left, JSType leftType, JSType resultType) {
491 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(resultType);
492 |     switch (left.getType()) {
493 |       case Token.NAME:
494 |         String varName = left.getString();
495 |         Var var = syntacticScope.getVar(varName);
496 |         if (var != null && var.isLocal() && var.getScope() != syntacticScope) {
497 |           assignedOuterLocalVars.put(var.getScope(), var);
498 |         }
499 | 
500 |         // When looking at VAR initializers for declared VARs, we trust
501 |         // the declared type over the type it's being initialized to.
502 |         // This has two purposes:
503 |         // 1) We avoid re-declaring declared variables so that built-in
504 |         //    types defined in externs are not redeclared.
505 |         // 2) When there's a lexical closure like
506 |         //    /** @type {?string} */ var x = null;
507 |         //    function f() { x = 'xyz'; }
508 |         //    the inference will ignore the lexical closure,
509 |         //    which is just wrong. This bug needs to be fixed eventually.
510 |         boolean isVarDeclaration = left.hasChildren();
511 |         if (!isVarDeclaration || var == null || var.isTypeInferred()) {
512 |           redeclare(scope, varName, resultType);
513 |         }
514 |         left.setJSType(isVarDeclaration || leftType == null ?
515 |             resultType : null);
516 | 
517 |         if (var != null && var.isTypeInferred()) {
518 |           JSType oldType = var.getType();
519 |           var.setType(oldType == null ?
520 |               resultType : oldType.getLeastSupertype(resultType));
521 |         }
522 |         break;
523 |       case Token.GETPROP:
524 |         String qualifiedName = left.getQualifiedName();
525 |         if (qualifiedName != null) {
526 |           scope.inferQualifiedSlot(qualifiedName,
527 |               leftType == null ? getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) : leftType,
528 |               resultType);
529 |         }
530 | 
531 |         left.setJSType(resultType);
532 |         ensurePropertyDefined(left, resultType);
533 |         break;
534 |     }
535 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.ensureTyped(NodeTraversal,Node,JSType)

Documentation:
/**
   * Enforces type casts, and ensures the node is typed.
   *
   * A cast in the way that we use it in JSDoc annotations never
   * alters the generated code and therefore never can induce any runtime
   * operation. What this means is that a 'cast' is really just a compile
   * time constraint on the underlying value. In the future, we may add
   * support for run-time casts for compiled tests.
   *
   * To ensure some shred of sanity, we enforce the notion that the
   * type you are casting to may only meaningfully be a narrower type
   * than the underlying declared type. We also invalidate optimizations
   * on bad type casts.
   *
   * @param t The traversal object needed to report errors.
   * @param n The node getting a type assigned to it.
   * @param type The type to be assigned.
   */
Method code:
1673 |   private void ensureTyped(NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType type) {
1674 |     // Make sure FUNCTION nodes always get function type.
1675 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() != Token.FUNCTION ||
1676 |             type instanceof FunctionType ||
1677 |             type.isUnknownType());
1678 |     JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1679 |     if (info != null) {
1680 |       if (info.hasType()) {
1681 |         JSType infoType = info.getType().evaluate(t.getScope());
1682 |         validator.expectCanCast(t, n, infoType, type);
1683 |         type = infoType;
1684 |       }
1685 | 
1686 |       if (info.isImplicitCast() && !inExterns) {
1687 |         String propName = n.getType() == Token.GETPROP ?
1688 |             n.getLastChild().getString() : "(missing)";
1689 |         compiler.report(
1690 |             JSError.make(t, n, ILLEGAL_IMPLICIT_CAST, propName));
1691 |       }
1692 |     }
1693 | 
1694 |     if (n.getJSType() == null) {
1695 |       n.setJSType(type);
1696 |     }
1697 |   }

146 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
147 |     this.root = root;

149 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();

151 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities);
152 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
153 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
154 | 
155 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
156 |     // search on the CFG.
157 |     priorityCounter = 0;
158 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
159 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
160 | 
161 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
162 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
163 |       // priority of them too.
164 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
165 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
166 |         if (value != null && value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
167 |           Preconditions.checkState(
168 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
169 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
170 |         }
171 |       }
172 |     }
173 | 
174 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
175 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
176 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
177 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
178 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
179 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
180 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
181 |       }
182 |     }
183 | 
184 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
185 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
186 |   }

/**
   * Create a map of constant names to constant values from a textual
   * description of the map.
   *
   * @param definitions A list of overriding definitions for defines in
   *     the form <name>[=<val>], where <val> is a number, boolean, or
   *     single-quoted string without single quotes.
   */
Method code:
1001 |   @VisibleForTesting
1002 |   static void createDefineReplacements(List<String> definitions,
1003 |       CompilerOptions options) {
1004 |     // Parse the definitions
1005 |     for (String override : definitions) {
1006 |       String[] assignment = override.split("=", 2);
1007 |       String defName = assignment[0];
1008 | 
1009 |       if (defName.length() > 0) {
1010 |         if (assignment.length == 1) {
1011 |           options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, true);
1012 |           continue;
1013 |         } else {
1014 |           String defValue = assignment[1];
1015 | 
1016 |           if (defValue.equals("true")) {
1017 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, true);
1018 |             continue;
1019 |           } else if (defValue.equals("false")) {
1020 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, false);
1021 |             continue;
1022 |           } else if (defValue.length() > 1 &&
1023 |               defValue.charAt(0) == '\'' &&
1024 |               defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\'') {
1025 |             // If the value starts and ends with a single quote,
1026 |             // we assume that it's a string.
1027 |             String maybeStringVal =
1028 |                 defValue.substring(1, defValue.length() - 1);
1029 |             if (maybeStringVal.indexOf('\'') == -1) {
1030 |               options.setDefineToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1031 |               continue;
1032 |             }
1033 |           } else {
1034 |             try {
1035 |               options.setDefineToDoubleLiteral(defName,
1036 |                   Double.parseDouble(defValue));
1037 |               continue;
1038 |             } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
1039 |               // do nothing, it will be caught at the end
1040 |             }
1041 |           }
1042 |         }
1043 |       }
1044 | 
1045 |       throw new RuntimeException(
1046 |           "--define flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1047 |     }
1048 |   }

/**
   * Merge a block with its parent block.
   * @return Whether the block was removed.
   */
Method code:
1104 |   static boolean tryMergeBlock(Node block) {
1105 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.getType() == Token.BLOCK);
1106 |     Node parent = block.getParent();
1107 |     // Try to remove the block if its parent is a block/script or if its
1108 |     // parent is label and it has exactly one child.
1109 |     if (NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {

1119 |       parent.replaceChild(block, block.removeFirstChild());
1120 |       return true;
1121 |     } else {
1122 |       return false;
1123 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FoldConstants.tryFoldStringJoin(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FoldConstants.java
Original range: 1461-1551
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';
   */
Method code:
1461 |   void tryFoldStringJoin(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node left, Node right,
1462 |                          Node parent) {
1463 |     if (!NodeUtil.isGetProp(left) || !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(right)) {
1464 |       return;
1465 |     }
1466 | 
1467 |     Node arrayNode = left.getFirstChild();
1468 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();
1469 | 
1470 |     if ((arrayNode.getType() != Token.ARRAYLIT) ||
1471 |         !functionName.getString().equals("join")) {
1472 |       return;
1473 |     }
1474 | 
1475 |     String joinString = NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
1476 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
1477 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
1478 |     int foldedSize = 0;
1479 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
1480 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
1481 |     while (elem != null) {
1482 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem)) {
1483 |         if (sb == null) {
1484 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
1485 |         } else {
1486 |           sb.append(joinString);
1487 |         }
1488 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getStringValue(elem));
1489 |       } else {
1490 |         if (sb != null) {
1491 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
1492 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
1493 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(Node.newString(sb.toString()));
1494 |           sb = null;
1495 |         }
1496 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
1497 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
1498 |       }
1499 |       elem = elem.getNext();
1500 |     }
1501 | 
1502 |     if (sb != null) {
1503 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
1504 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
1505 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(Node.newString(sb.toString()));
1506 |     }
1507 |     // one for each comma.
1508 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
1509 | 
1510 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
1511 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
1512 |       case 0:
1513 |         Node emptyStringNode = Node.newString("");
1514 |         parent.replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
1515 |         break;
1516 | 
1517 |       case 1:
1518 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
1519 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
1520 |           return;
1521 |         }
1522 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
1523 |         if (foldedStringNode.getType() != Token.STRING) {
1524 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
1525 |           // it is coerced to a string.
1526 |           Node replacement = new Node(Token.ADD,
1527 |               Node.newString(""), foldedStringNode);
1528 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
1529 |         }
1530 |         parent.replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
1531 |         break;
1532 | 
1533 |       default:
1534 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
1535 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
1536 |           return;
1537 |         }
1538 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
1539 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
1540 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right);
1541 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
1542 |           return;
1543 |         }
1544 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
1545 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
1546 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
1547 |         }
1548 |         break;
1549 |     }
1550 |     t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
1551 |   }

===== M1015 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(NodeTraversal,ControlFlowGraph<Node>,Set<Var>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 191-265
Documentation:

Method code:
191 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(
192 |       NodeTraversal t, ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg, Set<Var> escaped) {
193 |     UndiGraph<Var, Void> interferenceGraph =
194 |         new LinkedUndirectedGraph<Var, Void>();
195 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
196 | 
197 |     // First create a node for each non-escaped variable.
198 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = scope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
199 |       Var v = i.next();
200 |       if (!escaped.contains(v)) {
201 |         
202 |         // TODO(user): In theory, we CAN coalesce function names just like
203 |         // any variables. Our Liveness analysis captures this just like it as
204 |         // described in the specification. However, we saw some zipped and
205 |         // and unzipped size increase after this. We are not totally sure why
206 |         // that is but, for now, we will respect the dead functions and not play
207 |         // around with it.
208 |         if (!NodeUtil.isFunction(v.getParentNode())) {
209 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
210 |         }
211 |       }
212 |     }
213 | 
214 |     // Go through every single point of the program and look at each variable
215 |     // pairs. If they are both live at the same time, at an edge between them.
216 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
217 |       FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
218 |       if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
219 |         continue;
220 |       }
221 | 
222 |       int varsInScope = scope.getVarCount();
223 |       ArrayList<CombinedLiveRangeChecker> rangesToCheck =
224 |           new ArrayList<CombinedLiveRangeChecker>(
225 |               varsInScope * varsInScope);
226 | 
227 |       for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
228 |         Var v1 = i1.next();
229 |         for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
230 |           Var v2 = i2.next();
231 | 
232 |           if (v1 == v2 || !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
233 |               !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
234 |             // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
235 |             // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
236 |             continue;
237 |           }
238 | 
239 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
240 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
241 |           // Finally, check the live states and add edge when possible.
242 |           if (v1.getParentNode().getType() == Token.LP &&
243 |               v2.getParentNode().getType() == Token.LP) {
244 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
245 |           } else if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
246 |               (v1OutLive && v2OutLive)) {
247 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
248 |           } else {
249 |             LiveRangeChecker checker1 =
250 |                 new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2);
251 |             LiveRangeChecker checker2 =
252 |                 new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1);
253 |             rangesToCheck.add(new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(checker1, checker2));
254 |           }
255 |         }
256 |       }
257 | 
258 |       // Do the collected live range checks.
259 |       checkRanges(rangesToCheck, cfgNode.getValue());
260 |       for (CombinedLiveRangeChecker range : rangesToCheck) {
261 |         range.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph);
262 |       }
263 |     }
264 |     return interferenceGraph;
265 |   }

===== M1018 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runInCompilerThread(Callable<T>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 459-509
Documentation:

Method code:
459 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
460 |   private <T> T runInCompilerThread(final Callable<T> callable) {
461 | 
462 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the jscompiler overflows the stack when running on some
463 |     // large or complex js code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
464 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
465 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
466 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
467 | 
468 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = options_.tracer.isOn();
469 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
470 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
471 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
472 |       public void run() {
473 |         try {
474 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
475 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
476 |           }
477 |           result[0] = callable.call();
478 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
479 |           exception[0] = e;
480 |         } finally {
481 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
482 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
483 |           }
484 |         }
485 |       }
486 |     };
487 | 
488 |     if (useThreads) {
489 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
490 |       th.start();
491 |       while (true) {
492 |         try {
493 |           th.join();
494 |           break;
495 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
496 |           // ignore
497 |         }
498 |       }
499 |     } else {
500 |       runnable.run();
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
504 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
505 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
506 |     }
507 | 
508 |     return (T) result[0];
509 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal,Map<Var, ReferenceCollection>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 196-224
Documentation:
/**
     * For all variables in this scope, see if they are only used once.
     * If it looks safe to do so, inline them.
     */
Method code:
196 |     private void doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal t,
197 |         Map<Var, ReferenceCollection> referenceMap) {
198 | 
199 |       for (Iterator<Var> it = t.getScope().getVars(); it.hasNext();) {
200 |         Var v = it.next();
201 | 
202 |         ReferenceCollection referenceInfo = referenceMap.get(v);
203 | 
204 |         // referenceInfo will be null if we're in constants-only mode
205 |         // and the variable is not a constant.
206 |         if (referenceInfo == null || isVarInlineForbidden(v) ||
207 |             staleVars.contains(v)) {
208 |           // Never try to inline exported variables or variables that
209 |           // were not collected or variables that have already been inlined.
210 |           continue;
211 |         } else if (isInlineableDeclaredConstant(v, referenceInfo)) {
212 |           Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReferenceForConstants();
213 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
214 |           inlineDeclaredConstant(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
215 |           staleVars.add(v);
216 |         } else if (mode == Mode.CONSTANTS_ONLY) {
217 |           // If we're in constants-only mode, don't run more aggressive
218 |           // inlining heuristics. See InlineConstantsTest.
219 |           continue;
220 |         } else {
221 |           inlineNonConstants(v, referenceInfo);
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |     }

/**
   * Since this pass reports errors only when a global {@code this} keyword
   * is encountered, there is no reason to traverse non global contexts.
   */
Method code:
82 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
83 |     
84 |     if (n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
85 |       // Don't traverse functions that are constructors or have the @this
86 |       // annotation.
87 |       JSDocInfo jsDoc = getFunctionJsDocInfo(n);
88 |       if (jsDoc != null && (jsDoc.isConstructor() || jsDoc.hasThisType())) {
89 |         return false;
90 |       }
91 |     }
92 |     
93 |     if (parent != null && parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
94 |       Node lhs = parent.getFirstChild();
95 |       Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
96 |       
97 |       if (n == lhs) {
98 |         // Always traverse the left side of the assignment. To handle
99 |         // nested assignments properly (e.g., (a = this).property = c;),
100 |         // assignLhsChild should not be overridden.
101 |         if (assignLhsChild == null) {
102 |           assignLhsChild = lhs;
103 |         }
104 |       } else {
105 |         // Only traverse the right side if it's not an assignment to a prototype
106 |         // property or subproperty.
107 |         if (lhs.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
108 |           if (lhs.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
109 |             return false;
110 |           }
111 |           String leftName = lhs.getQualifiedName();
112 |           if (leftName != null && leftName.contains(".prototype.")) {
113 |             return false;
114 |           }
115 |         }
116 |       }
117 |     }
118 |     
119 |     return true;
120 |   }

/**
   * Connects two nodes in the graph with an edge if such edge does not already
   * exists between the nodes.
   *
   * @param n1 First node.
   * @param edge The edge.
   * @param n2 Second node.
   */
Method code:
121 |   public final void connectIfNotFound(N n1, E edge, N n2) {
122 |     GraphNode<N, E> node1 = getNode(n1);
123 |     GraphNode<N, E> node2 = getNode(n2);
124 |     if (node1 == null) {
125 |       throw new IllegalArgumentException(n1 + " does not exist in graph");
126 |     }
127 |     if (node2 == null) {
128 |       throw new IllegalArgumentException(n2 + " does not exist in graph");
129 |     }

131 |     for (GraphEdge<N, E> e : edgeList) {

133 |       if (e.getValue() == edge || e.getValue().equals(edge)) {
134 |         return;

136 |     }

   * This is the meat of the type checking.  It is basically one big switch,
   * with each case representing one type of parse tree node.  The individual
   * cases are usually pretty straightforward.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   * @param parent The parent of the node n.

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.ArrowType.equals(Object)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/ArrowType.java
Original range: 139-187
Documentation:

Method code:
139 |   @Override
140 |   public boolean equals(Object object) {
141 |     // Please keep this method in sync with the hashCode() method below.
142 |     if (!(object instanceof ArrowType)) {
143 |       return false;
144 |     }
145 |     ArrowType that = (ArrowType) object;
146 |     // if both return types are specified, then they should be equal
147 |     if (returnType == null) {
148 |       if (that.returnType != null) {
149 |         return false;
150 |       }
151 |     } else {
152 |       if (that.returnType == null) {
153 |         return false;
154 |       }
155 |       if (!returnType.equals(that.returnType)) {
156 |         return false;
157 |       }
158 |     }
159 |     // if both types include parameters, the lists should be the same
160 |     if (parameters == null) {
161 |       return that.parameters == null;
162 |     } else if (that.parameters == null) {
163 |       return false;
164 |     }
165 |     Node thisParam = parameters.getFirstChild();
166 |     Node otherParam = that.parameters.getFirstChild();
167 |     while (thisParam != null && otherParam != null) {
168 |       JSType thisParamType = thisParam.getJSType();
169 |       JSType otherParamType = otherParam.getJSType();
170 |       if (thisParamType != null) {
171 |         // Both parameter lists give a type for this param, it should be equal
172 |         if (otherParamType != null &&
173 |             !thisParamType.equals(otherParamType)) {
174 |           return false;
175 |         }
176 |       } else {
177 |         if (otherParamType != null) {
178 |           return false;
179 |         }
180 |       }
181 |       thisParam = thisParam.getNext();
182 |       otherParam = otherParam.getNext();
183 |     }
184 |     // One of the parameters is null, so the types are only equal if both
185 |     // parameter lists are null (they are equal).
186 |     return thisParam == otherParam;
187 |   }
