226 |     private void inlineNonConstants(
227 |         Var v, ReferenceCollection referenceInfo) {
228 |       int refCount = referenceInfo.references.size();
229 |       Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
230 |       Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
231 |       int firstRefAfterInit = (declaration == init) ? 2 : 3;
232 | 
233 |       if (refCount > 1 &&
234 |           isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(v, referenceInfo)) {
235 |         // if the variable is referenced more than once, we can only
236 |         // inline it if it's immutable and never defined before referenced.
237 |         Node value;
238 |         if (init != null) {
239 |           value = init.getAssignedValue();
240 |         } else {
241 |           // Create a new node for variable that is never initialized.
242 |           value = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode();
243 |         }
244 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
245 |         inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
246 |         staleVars.add(v);
247 |       } else if (refCount == firstRefAfterInit) {
248 |         // The variable likely only read once, try some more
249 |         // complex inlining heuristics.
250 |         Reference reference = referenceInfo.references.get(
251 |             firstRefAfterInit - 1);
252 |         if (canInline(declaration, init, reference)) {
253 |           inline(v, declaration, init, reference);
254 |           staleVars.add(v);
255 |         }
256 |       } else if (declaration != init && refCount == 2) {
257 |         if (isValidDeclaration(declaration) && isValidInitialization(init)) {
258 |           // The only reference is the initialization, remove the assignment and
259 |           // the variable declaration.
260 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
261 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
262 |           inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
263 |           staleVars.add(v);
264 |         }
265 |       }
266 | 
267 |       // If this variable was not inlined normally, check if we can
268 |       // inline an alias of it. (If the variable was inlined, then the
269 |       // reference data is out of sync. We're better off just waiting for
270 |       // the next pass.)
271 |       if (!staleVars.contains(v) && referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&
272 |           referenceInfo.isAssignedOnce()) {
273 |         List<Reference> refs = referenceInfo.references;
274 |         for (int i = 1 /* start from a read */; i < refs.size(); i++) {
275 |           Node nameNode = refs.get(i).getNameNode();
276 |           if (aliasCandidates.containsKey(nameNode)) {
277 |             AliasCandidate candidate = aliasCandidates.get(nameNode);
278 |             if (!staleVars.contains(candidate.alias)) {
279 |               Reference aliasInit;
280 |               aliasInit = candidate.refInfo.getInitializingReference();
281 |               Node value = aliasInit.getAssignedValue();
282 |               Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
283 |               inlineWellDefinedVariable(candidate.alias,
284 |                   value,
285 |                   candidate.refInfo.references);
286 |               staleVars.add(candidate.alias);
287 |             }

/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * function() { return a; } is not.
   */
Method code:
205 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n) {
206 |     // TODO(nicksantos): Refine this function to catch more literals.
207 |     switch (n.getType()) {
208 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
209 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
210 |       case Token.REGEXP:
211 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
212 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
213 |              child = child.getNext()) {
214 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child)) {
215 |             return false;
216 |           }
217 |         }
218 |         return true;
219 | 
220 |       default:
221 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
222 |     }
223 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.visitReturn(NodeTraversal,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java

Documentation:
/**
   * Visits a RETURN node.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   */
Method code:
1434 |   private void visitReturn(NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
1435 |     Node function = t.getEnclosingFunction();
1436 | 
1437 |     // This is a misplaced return, but the real JS will fail to compile,
1438 |     // so let it go.
1439 |     if (function == null) {
1440 |       return;
1441 |     }
1442 |     JSType jsType = getJSType(function);
1443 | 
1444 |     if (jsType instanceof FunctionType) {
1445 |       FunctionType functionType = (FunctionType) jsType;
1446 | 
1447 |       JSType returnType = functionType.getReturnType();
1448 | 
1449 |       // if no return type is specified, undefined must be returned
1450 |       // (it's a void function)
1451 |       if (returnType == null) {
1452 |         returnType = getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);
1453 |       }
1454 | 
1455 |       // fetching the returned value's type
1456 |       Node valueNode = n.getFirstChild();
1457 |       JSType actualReturnType;
1458 |       if (valueNode == null) {
1459 |         actualReturnType = getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);
1460 |         valueNode = n;
1461 |       } else {
1462 |         actualReturnType = getJSType(valueNode);
1463 |       }
1464 | 
1465 |       // verifying
1466 |       validator.expectCanAssignTo(t, valueNode, actualReturnType, returnType,
1467 |           "inconsistent return type");
1468 |     }
1469 |   }

/**
   * Informally, a function is represented by
   * {@code function (params): returnType} where the {@code params} is a comma
   * separated list of types, the first one being a special
   * {@code this:T} if the function expects a known type for {@code this}.
   */
Method code:
654 |   @Override
655 |   public String toString() {
656 |     if (this == registry.getNativeType(JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_INSTANCE_TYPE)) {
657 |       return "Function";
658 |     }
659 | 
660 |     StringBuilder b = new StringBuilder(32);
661 |     b.append("function (");
662 |     int paramNum = (call == null || call.parameters == null) ?
663 |         0 : call.parameters.getChildCount();
664 |     boolean hasKnownTypeOfThis = !typeOfThis.isUnknownType();
665 |     if (hasKnownTypeOfThis) {
666 |       b.append("this:");
667 |       b.append(typeOfThis.toString());
668 |     }
669 |     if (paramNum > 0) {
670 |       if (hasKnownTypeOfThis) {
671 |         b.append(", ");
672 |       }
673 |       Node p = call.parameters.getFirstChild();
674 |       if (p.isVarArgs()) {
675 |         appendVarArgsString(b, p.getJSType());
676 |       } else {
677 |         b.append(p.getJSType().toString());
678 |       }
679 |       p = p.getNext();
680 |       while (p != null) {
681 |         b.append(", ");
682 |         if (p.isVarArgs()) {
683 |           appendVarArgsString(b, p.getJSType());
684 |         } else {
685 |           b.append(p.getJSType().toString());
686 |         }
687 |         p = p.getNext();
688 |       }
689 |     }
690 |     b.append(")");
691 |     if (call != null && call.returnType != null) {
692 |       b.append(": ");
693 |       b.append(call.returnType);
694 |     }
695 |     return b.toString();
696 |   }

/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
85 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
86 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
87 |     // just bail out early here.
88 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
89 |       return this;
90 |     }
91 | 
92 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
93 | 
94 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
95 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
96 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
97 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
98 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
99 |     }
100 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
101 |       if (alternate instanceof UnionType) {
102 |         UnionType union = (UnionType) alternate;
103 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
104 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
105 |         }
106 |       } else {
107 |         if (!alternate.isUnknownType()) {
108 |           Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
109 |           while (it.hasNext()) {
110 |             JSType current = it.next();
111 |             if (!current.isUnknownType()) {
112 |               if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
113 |                 // Alternate is unnecessary.
114 |                 return this;
115 |               } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
116 |                 // Alternate makes current obsolete
117 |                 it.remove();
118 |               }
119 |             }
120 |           }
121 |         }
122 |         alternates.add(alternate);
123 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
124 |       }
125 |     } else {
126 |       result = null;
127 |     }
128 |     return this;
129 |   }

/**
   * Split a var node such as:
   *   var a, b;
   * into individual statements:
   *   var a;
   *   var b;
   * @param n The whose children we should inspect.
   */
Method code:
354 |   private void splitVarDeclarations(Node n) {
355 |     for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
356 |       next = c.getNext();
357 |       if (c.getType() == Token.VAR) {
358 |         if (assertOnChange && !c.hasChildren()) {
359 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Empty VAR node.");
360 |         }
361 | 
362 |         while (c.getFirstChild() != c.getLastChild()) {
363 |           Node name = c.getFirstChild();
364 |           c.removeChild(name);
365 |           Node newVar = new Node(Token.VAR, name, n.getLineno(), n.getCharno());
366 |           n.addChildBefore(newVar, c);
367 |           reportCodeChange("VAR with multiple children");
368 |         }
369 |       }
370 |     }
371 |   }

244 |     @Override
245 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node node, Node parent) {
246 |       if (node.getType() == Token.NAME) {
247 |         String oldName = node.getString();
248 |         if (oldName.indexOf("$$") != -1) {
249 |           Scope scope = t.getScope();
250 |           Var var = t.getScope().getVar(oldName);
251 |           if (var == null || var.isGlobal()) {
252 |             return;
253 |           }
254 | 
255 |           if (nameMap.containsKey(var)) {
256 |             node.setString(nameMap.get(var));
257 |           } else {
258 |             String newName = oldName.substring(0, oldName.lastIndexOf("$$"));
259 | 
260 |             // Before we change the name of this variable, double-check to
261 |             // make sure we're not declaring a duplicate name in the
262 |             // same scope as the var declaration.
263 |             if (var.scope.isDeclared(newName, false) ||
264 |                 !TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(newName)) {
265 |               newName = oldName;
266 |             } else {
267 |               var.scope.declare(newName, var.nameNode, null, null);
268 | 
269 |               // Handle bleeding functions.
270 |               Node parentNode = var.getParentNode();
271 |               if (parentNode.getType() == Token.FUNCTION &&
272 |                   parentNode == var.scope.getRootNode()) {
273 |                 var.getNameNode().setString(newName);
274 |               }
275 | 
276 |               node.setString(newName);
277 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
278 |             }
279 | 
280 |             nameMap.put(var, newName);
281 |           }
282 |         }
283 |       }
284 |     }

/**
   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.
   * @param silence_threshold Traces for time less than silence_threshold
   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran
   */
Method code:
421 |   long stop(int silence_threshold) {
422 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
423 | 
424 |     ThreadTrace trace = getThreadTrace();
425 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
426 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
427 |       return 0;
428 |     }
429 | 
430 |     stopTimeMs = clock.currentTimeMillis();
431 |     if (extraTracingValues != null) {
432 |       // We use extraTracingValues.length rather than extraTracingStatistics.size() because
433 |       // a new statistic may have been added
434 |       for (int i = 0; i < extraTracingValues.length; i++) {
435 |         long value = extraTracingStatistics.get(i).stop(startThread);
436 |         extraTracingValues[i] = value - extraTracingValues[i];
437 |       }
438 |     }
439 | 
440 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
441 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
442 |       return 0;
443 |     }
444 | 
445 |     trace.endEvent(this, silence_threshold);
446 |     return stopTimeMs - startTimeMs;
447 |   }

/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in javascript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
607 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
608 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
609 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
610 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
611 |       @Override
612 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
613 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !NodeUtil.isName(n)
614 |             || NodeUtil.isFunction(parent)) {
615 |           return;
616 |         }
617 |         String name = n.getString();
618 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
619 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
620 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
621 |         }
622 |       }
623 |     };
624 | 
625 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
626 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
627 | 
628 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
629 |     //    begin with.
630 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
631 |       Var var = i.next();
632 |       if (var.getParentNode().getType() == Token.CATCH ||
633 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
634 |         escaped.add(var);
635 |       }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.ProcessVars.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Method code:
170 |     @Override
171 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
172 |       if (n.getType() != Token.NAME) {
173 |         return;
174 |       }
175 | 
176 |       String name = n.getString();
177 | 
178 |       // Ignore anonymous functions
179 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
180 |         return;
181 |       }
182 | 
183 |       // Is this local or Global?
184 |       Scope.Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
185 |       boolean local = (var != null) && var.isLocal();
186 | 
187 |       // Are we renaming global variables?
188 |       if (!local && localRenamingOnly) {
189 |         reservedNames.add(name);
190 |         return;
191 |       }
192 | 
193 |       // Are we renaming anonymous function names?
194 |       if (preserveAnonymousFunctionNames
195 |           && var != null
196 |           && NodeUtil.isAnonymousFunction(var.getParentNode())) {
197 |         reservedNames.add(name);
198 |         return;
199 |       }
200 | 
201 |       // Check if we can rename this.
202 |       if (!okToRenameVar(name, local)) {
203 |         return;
204 |       }
205 | 
206 |       if (isExternsPass_) {
207 |         // Keep track of extern globals.
208 |         if (!local) {
209 |           externNames.add(name);
210 |         }
211 |         return;
212 |       }
213 | 
214 |       if (local) {
215 |         // Local var: assign a new name
216 |         String tempName = LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX + var.getLocalVarIndex();
217 |         incCount(tempName, null);
218 |         localNameNodes.add(n);
219 |         localTempNames.add(tempName);
220 |       } else if (var != null) {  // Not an extern
221 |         // If it's global, increment global count
222 |         incCount(name, var.input);
223 |         globalNameNodes.add(n);
224 |       }

===== M1190 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Original range: 88-118
Documentation:

Method code:
88 |   @Override
89 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
90 |     if (parent == null) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 |     if (n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION || n.getType() == Token.SCRIPT) {
94 |       return;
95 |     }
96 |     // Removes TRYs that had its CATCH removed and/or empty FINALLY.
97 |     if (n.getType() == Token.TRY) {
98 |       Node body = n.getFirstChild();
99 |       Node catchOrFinallyBlock = body.getNext();
100 |       Node finallyBlock = catchOrFinallyBlock.getNext();
101 | 
102 |       if (!catchOrFinallyBlock.hasChildren() &&
103 |           (finallyBlock == null || !finallyBlock.hasChildren())) {
104 |         n.removeChild(body);
105 |         parent.replaceChild(n, body);
106 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
107 |         n = body;
108 |       }
109 |     }
110 |     GraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getNode(n);
111 |     if (gNode == null) { // Not in CFG.
112 |       return;
113 |     }
114 |     if (gNode.getAnnotation() != GraphReachability.REACHABLE ||
115 |         (removeNoOpStatements && !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n))) {
116 |       removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n, parent);
117 |     }
118 |   }

/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.
     */
Method code:
743 |     void replace() {
744 |       if (firstNode == null) {
745 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
746 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
747 |         return;
748 |       }
749 | 
750 |       // Handle the case where there is a duplicate definition for an explicitly
751 |       // provided symbol.
752 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
753 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
754 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
755 | 
756 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
757 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
758 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(candidateDefinition)) {
759 |           candidateDefinition.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_NAMESPACE, true);
760 |           Node assignNode = candidateDefinition.getFirstChild();
761 |           Node nameNode = assignNode.getFirstChild();
762 |           if (nameNode.getType() == Token.NAME) {
763 |             // Need to convert this assign to a var declaration.
764 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();
765 |             assignNode.removeChild(nameNode);
766 |             assignNode.removeChild(valueNode);
767 |             nameNode.addChildToFront(valueNode);
768 |             Node varNode = new Node(Token.VAR, nameNode);
769 |             varNode.copyInformationFrom(candidateDefinition);
770 |             candidateDefinition.getParent().replaceChild(
771 |                 candidateDefinition, varNode);
772 |             nameNode.setJSDocInfo(assignNode.getJSDocInfo());
773 |             compiler.reportCodeChange();
774 |             replacementNode = varNode;
775 |           }
776 |         }
777 |       } else {
778 |         // Handle the case where there's not a duplicate definition.
779 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();
780 |         if (firstModule == minimumModule) {
781 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
782 |         } else {
783 |           // In this case, the name was implicitly provided by two independent
784 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.
785 |           int indexOfDot = namespace.indexOf('.');
786 |           if (indexOfDot == -1) {
787 |             // Any old place is fine.
788 |             compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(minimumModule)
789 |                 .addChildToBack(replacementNode);
790 |           } else {
791 |             // Add it after the parent namespace.
792 |             ProvidedName parentName =

794 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName);
795 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName.replacementNode);

254 |   @Override
255 |   public boolean equals(Object other) {
256 |     if (other instanceof LinkedFlowScope) {
257 |       LinkedFlowScope that = (LinkedFlowScope) other;
258 |       if (this.optimize() == that.optimize()) {
259 |         return true;
260 |       }
261 | 
262 |       // If two flow scopes are in the same function, then they could have
263 |       // two possible function scopes: the real one and the BOTTOM scope.
264 |       // If they have different function scopes, we *should* iterate thru all
265 |       // the variables in each scope and compare. However, 99.9% of the time,
266 |       // they're not equal. And the other .1% of the time, we can pretend
267 |       // they're equal--this just means that data flow analysis will have
268 |       // to propagate the entry lattice a little bit further than it
269 |       // really needs to. Everything will still come out ok.
270 |       if (this.getFunctionScope() != that.getFunctionScope()) {
271 |         return false;
272 |       }
273 | 
274 |       if (cache == that.cache) {
275 |         // If the two flow scopes have the same cache, then we can check
276 |         // equality a lot faster: by just looking at the "dirty" elements
277 |         // in the cache, and comparing them in both scopes.
278 |         for (String name : cache.dirtySymbols) {
279 |           if (diffSlots(getSlot(name), that.getSlot(name))) {
280 |             return false;
281 |           }
282 |         }
283 | 
284 |         return true;
285 |       }
286 | 
287 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> myFlowSlots = allFlowSlots();
288 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> otherFlowSlots = that.allFlowSlots();
289 | 
290 |       for (StaticSlot<JSType> slot : myFlowSlots.values()) {
291 |         if (diffSlots(slot, otherFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
292 |           return false;
293 |         }
294 |         otherFlowSlots.remove(slot.getName());
295 |       }
296 |       for (StaticSlot<JSType> slot : otherFlowSlots.values()) {
297 |         if (diffSlots(slot, myFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
298 |           return false;
299 |         }
300 |       }
301 |       return true;
302 |     }

===== M1210 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 149-194
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
149 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
150 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
151 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
152 |       case Token.BLOCK:
153 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
154 |       case Token.TRY:
155 |       case Token.FINALLY:
156 |         return true;
157 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
158 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
159 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
160 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
161 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
162 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
163 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
164 |         // child.
165 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
166 |       case Token.WHILE:
167 |       case Token.DO:
168 |       case Token.IF:
169 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
170 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
171 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
172 |         
173 |       case Token.FOR:
174 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
175 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
176 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
177 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
178 |         // That way the following:
179 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
180 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
181 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
182 |           return n == parent.getLastChild(); 
183 |         } else {
184 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
185 |         }
186 |       case Token.SWITCH:
187 |       case Token.CASE:
188 |       case Token.CATCH:
189 |       case Token.WITH:
190 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
191 |       default:
192 |         return false;
193 |     }
194 |   }

===== M1232 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.Node.isEquivalentTo(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/Node.java
Original range: 1543-1577
Documentation:
/** Returns true if this node is equivalent semantically to another */
Method code:
1543 |     public boolean isEquivalentTo(Node node) {
1544 |         if (type == Token.ARRAYLIT) {
1545 |             try {
1546 |                 int[] indices1 = (int[])getProp(Node.SKIP_INDEXES_PROP);
1547 |                 int[] indices2 = (int[])node.getProp(Node.SKIP_INDEXES_PROP);
1548 |                 if (indices1 == null) {
1549 |                     if (indices2 != null)
1550 |                         return false;
1551 |                 } else if (indices2 == null) {
1552 |                     return false;
1553 |                 } else if (indices1.length != indices2.length) {
1554 |                     return false;
1555 |                 } else {
1556 |                     for (int i = 0; i < indices1.length; i++) {
1557 |                         if (indices1[i] != indices2[i])
1558 |                             return false;
1559 |                     }
1560 |                 }
1561 |             } catch (Exception e) {
1562 |                 return false;
1563 |             }
1564 |         } else if (type == Token.INC ||
1565 |                    type == Token.DEC) {
1566 |             int post1 = this.getIntProp(INCRDECR_PROP, 0);
1567 |             int post2 = node.getIntProp(INCRDECR_PROP, 0);
1568 |             if (post1 != post2)
1569 |                 return false;
1570 |         } else if (type == Token.STRING) {
1571 |             int quoted1 = this.getIntProp(QUOTED_PROP, 0);
1572 |             int quoted2 = node.getIntProp(QUOTED_PROP, 0);
1573 |             if (quoted1 != quoted2)
1574 |                 return false;
1575 |         }
1576 |         return true;

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 112-205
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
112 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
113 | 
114 |     // Just an 'exit'.
115 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
116 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
117 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
118 |       return;
119 |     }
120 | 
121 |     // Just an 'if'.
122 |     if (n.getType() == Token.IF) {
123 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
124 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
125 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
126 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
127 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
128 |       }
129 |       return;
130 |     }
131 | 
132 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
133 |     if (n.getType() == Token.TRY) {
134 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
135 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
136 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
137 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
138 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
139 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
140 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
141 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
142 |       }
143 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
144 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
145 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
146 |       }
147 |     }
148 | 
149 |     // Just a 'label'.
150 |     if (n.getType() == Token.LABEL) {
151 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
152 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
153 |     }
154 | 
155 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
156 | 
157 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
158 |     if (n.getType() != Token.BLOCK || n.getLastChild() == null) {
159 |       return;
160 |     }
161 | 
162 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
163 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
164 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
165 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
166 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
167 | 
168 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
169 |       if (c.getType() == Token.IF) {
170 |         Node ifTree = c;
171 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
172 | 
173 |         // First, the true condition block.
174 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
175 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
176 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
177 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
178 | 
179 |         // Now the else block.
180 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
181 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
182 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
183 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
184 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
185 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
186 |         }
187 |       }
188 | 
189 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
190 |         break;
191 |       }
192 |     }
193 | 
194 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
195 |     // look at what has become the last child.
196 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
197 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
198 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
199 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
200 |         break;
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 | 
204 |     return;
205 |   }

     * {@link JSDocInfo}.
     * @param name the function's name

     * @param info the {@link JSDocInfo} attached to the function definition

480 |           rValue.getFirstChild().getNext() : null;
481 | 
482 |       if (functionType == null && info != null && info.hasType()) {
483 |         JSType type = info.getType().evaluate(scope);
484 | 
485 |         // Known to be not null since we have the FUNCTION token there.
486 |         type = type.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
487 |         if (type.isFunctionType()) {
488 |           functionType = (FunctionType) type;
489 |           functionType.setJSDocInfo(info);
490 |         }
491 |       }
492 | 
493 |       if (functionType == null) {
494 |         if (info == null ||
495 |             !FunctionTypeBuilder.isFunctionTypeDeclaration(info)) {
496 |           // We don't really have any type information in the annotation.
497 |           // Before we give up on this function, look at the object we're
498 |           // assigning it to. For example, if the function looks like this:
499 |           // SubFoo.prototype.bar = function() { ... };
500 |           // We can use type information on Foo.prototype.bar and apply it
501 |           // to this function.
502 |           if (lvalueNode != null && lvalueNode.getType() == Token.GETPROP &&
503 |               lvalueNode.isQualifiedName()) {
504 |             Var var = scope.getVar(
505 |                 lvalueNode.getFirstChild().getQualifiedName());
506 |             if (var != null) {
507 |               ObjectType ownerType = ObjectType.cast(var.getType());
508 |               FunctionType propType = null;
509 |               if (ownerType != null) {
510 |                 propType = findOverriddenFunction(
511 |                     ownerType, lvalueNode.getLastChild().getString());
512 |               }
513 | 
514 |               if (propType != null) {
515 |                 functionType =
516 |                     new FunctionTypeBuilder(
517 |                         name, compiler, errorRoot, sourceName, scope)
518 |                     .setSourceNode(fnRoot)
519 |                     .inferFromOverriddenFunction(propType, parametersNode)
520 |                     .inferThisType(info, owner)
521 |                     .buildAndRegister();
522 |               }
523 |             }
524 |           }
525 |         }
526 |       } // end if (functionType == null)
527 | 
528 |       if (functionType == null) {
529 |         functionType =
530 |             new FunctionTypeBuilder(name, compiler, errorRoot, sourceName,
531 |                 scope)
532 |             .setSourceNode(fnRoot)
533 |             .inferTemplateTypeName(info)
534 |             .inferReturnType(info)
535 |             .inferInheritance(info)
536 |             .inferThisType(info, owner)
537 |             .inferParameterTypes(parametersNode, info)
538 |             .buildAndRegister();
539 |       }
540 | 
541 |       // assigning the function type to the function node
542 |       if (rValue != null) {
543 |         rValue.setJSType(functionType);
544 |       }
545 | 
546 |       // all done
547 |       return functionType;
548 |     }

/**
   * Try to remove useless assignments from a control flow graph that has been
   * annotated with liveness information.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal.
   * @param cfg The control flow graph of the program annotated with liveness
   *        information.
   */
Method code:
96 |   private void tryRemoveDeadAssignments(NodeTraversal t,
97 |       ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg) {
98 |     List<DiGraphNode<Node, Branch>> nodes = cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes();
99 | 
100 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : nodes) {
101 |       FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state =
102 |           cfgNode.getAnnotation();
103 |       Node n = cfgNode.getValue();
104 |       if (n == null) {
105 |         continue;
106 |       }
107 |       switch (n.getType()) {
108 |         case Token.IF:
109 |         case Token.WHILE:
110 |         case Token.DO:
111 |           tryRemoveAssignment(t, NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), state);
112 |           continue;
113 |         case Token.FOR:
114 |           if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
115 |             tryRemoveAssignment(

117 |           }
118 |           continue;
119 |         case Token.SWITCH:
120 |         case Token.CASE:
121 |         case Token.RETURN:
122 |           if (n.hasChildren()) {
123 |             tryRemoveAssignment(t, n.getFirstChild(), state);
124 |           }
125 |           continue;
126 |         // TODO(user): case Token.VAR: Remove var a=1;a=2;.....
127 |       }
128 |       
129 |       tryRemoveAssignment(t, n, state);
130 |     }
131 |   }

   * "exits":

   * @param type The Token type to look for.

===== M1296 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 179-291
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
179 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
180 | 
181 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
182 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.getType() == Token.LP);
183 | 
184 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
185 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
186 |     boolean changed = false;
187 | 
188 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
189 |     // array.
190 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
191 | 
192 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
193 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
194 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
195 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
196 | 
197 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
198 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
199 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
200 | 
201 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
202 |       
203 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
204 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
205 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
206 |       if (getElem.getType() != Token.GETELEM) {
207 |         return false;
208 |       }
209 | 
210 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
211 | 
212 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
213 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
214 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
215 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
216 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
217 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
218 |         // it is never 'callee'.
219 |         return false; // Give up.
220 |       }
221 |       
222 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
223 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
224 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
225 |       if (NodeUtil.isCall(getElemParent) &&
226 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
227 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
228 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
229 |         return false;
230 |       }
231 | 
232 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
233 |       // than all the one we saw before.
234 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
235 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
236 |         highestIndex = value;
237 |       }
238 |     }
239 | 
240 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
241 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
242 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
243 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
244 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
245 | 
246 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
247 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
248 | 
249 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
250 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
251 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
252 |       String name = getNewName();
253 |       argNames[i] = name;
254 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(Node.newString(Token.NAME, name));
255 |       changed = true;
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
259 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
260 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
261 | 
262 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
263 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
264 |         continue;
265 |       }
266 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
267 | 
268 |       // Unnamed parameter.
269 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
270 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
271 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
272 |       } else {
273 |

/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced. Functions create their own scope, so we don't
   * recurse into them unless they are called.
   */
Method code:
115 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
116 |     int type = n.getType();
117 |     switch (type) {
118 |       // We traverse a function only if the function definition is
119 |       // immediately being referenced, e.g.
120 |       // - return function() { ... };
121 |       // - foo( function() { ... } )
122 |       // - array[ function() { ... } ];
123 |       //
124 |       // Otherwise we traverse into the function only when we encounter
125 |       // a reference to it (see markReferencedVar())
126 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
127 |         // If it's an exported function, or an anonymous function, assume
128 |         // that it'll be called.
129 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionAnonymous(n) ||
130 |             compiler_.getCodingConvention().isExported(
131 |                 n.getFirstChild().getString())) {
132 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.NAME:
137 |         if (parent.getType() != Token.VAR) {
138 |           // All non-var declarations are references to other vars
139 |           Var var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
140 |           if (var != null) {
141 |             markReferencedVar(var);
142 |           }
143 |         }
144 |         break;
145 |     }
146 | 
147 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
148 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
149 |     }
150 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 177-276

Method code:
177 |   @Override
178 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
179 |   List<FlowScope> branchedFlowThrough(Node source, FlowScope input) {
180 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, we just treat ON_EX edges like UNCOND
181 |     // edges. If we wanted to be perfect, we'd actually JOIN all the out
182 |     // lattices of this flow with the in lattice, and then make that the out
183 |     // lattice for the ON_EX edge. But it's probably to expensive to be
184 |     // worthwhile.
185 |     FlowScope output = flowThrough(source, input);
186 |     Node condition = null;
187 |     FlowScope conditionFlowScope = null;
188 |     BooleanOutcomePair conditionOutcomes = null;
189 | 
190 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> branchEdges = getCfg().getOutEdges(source);
191 |     List<FlowScope> result = Lists.newArrayListWithCapacity(branchEdges.size());
192 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> branchEdge : branchEdges) {
193 |       Branch branch = branchEdge.getValue();
194 |       FlowScope newScope = output;
195 | 
196 |       switch (branch) {
197 |         case ON_TRUE:
198 |           if (NodeUtil.isForIn(source)) {
199 |             // item is assigned a property name, so its type should be string.
200 |             Node item = source.getFirstChild();
201 |             if (item.getType() == Token.VAR) {
202 |               item = item.getFirstChild();
203 |             }
204 |             if (item.getType() == Token.NAME) {
205 |               FlowScope informed = output.createChildFlowScope();
206 |               redeclare(informed, item.getString(),
207 |                   getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
208 |               newScope = informed;
209 |             }
210 |             break;
211 |           }
212 | 
213 |           // FALL THROUGH
214 | 
215 |         case ON_FALSE:
216 |           if (condition == null) {
217 |             condition = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(source);
218 |             if (condition == null && source.getType() == Token.CASE) {
219 |               condition = source;
220 | 
221 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
222 |               // of the loop.
223 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
224 |                 conditionFlowScope = traverse(
225 |                     condition.getFirstChild(), output.createChildFlowScope());
226 |               }
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 | 
230 |           if (condition != null) {
231 |             if (condition.getType() == Token.AND ||
232 |                 condition.getType() == Token.OR) {
233 |               // When handling the short-circuiting binary operators,
234 |               // the outcome scope on true can be different than the outcome
235 |               // scope on false.
236 |               //
237 |               // TODO(nicksantos): The "right" way to do this is to
238 |               // carry the known outcome all the way through the
239 |               // recursive traversal, so that we can construct a
240 |               // different flow scope based on the outcome. However,
241 |               // this would require a bunch of code and a bunch of
242 |               // extra computation for an edge case. This seems to be
243 |               // a "good enough" approximation.
244 | 
245 |               // conditionOutcomes is cached from previous iterations
246 |               // of the loop.
247 |               if (conditionOutcomes == null) {
248 |                 conditionOutcomes = condition.getType() == Token.AND ?
249 |                     traverseAnd(condition, output.createChildFlowScope()) :
250 |                     traverseOr(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
251 |               }
252 |               newScope =
253 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
254 |                       condition,
255 |                       conditionOutcomes.getOutcomeFlowScope(
256 |                           condition.getType(), branch == Branch.ON_TRUE),
257 |                       branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
258 |             } else {
259 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
260 |               // of the loop.
261 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
262 |                 conditionFlowScope =
263 |                     traverse(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
264 |               }
265 |               newScope =
266 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
267 |                       condition, conditionFlowScope, branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
268 |             }
269 |           }
270 |           break;
271 |       }
272 | 
273 |       result.add(newScope.optimize());
274 |     }
275 |     return result;
276 |   }

128 |         // Dereference the type. If the result is not an object, or already
129 |         // has docs attached, then do nothing.
130 |         ObjectType objType = dereferenceToObject(varType);
131 |         if (objType == null || objType.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
132 |           return;
133 |         }
134 | 
135 |         attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(objType, docInfo, n.getString());
136 |         break;
137 | 
138 |       case Token.GETPROP:
139 |         // Infer JSDocInfo on properties.
140 |         // There are two ways to write doc comments on a property.
141 |         //
142 |         // 1)
143 |         // /** @deprecated */
144 |         // obj.prop = ...
145 |         //
146 |         // 2)
147 |         // /** @deprecated */
148 |         // obj.prop;
149 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(parent) ||
150 |             (parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
151 |              parent.getFirstChild() == n)) {
152 |           docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
153 |           if (docInfo == null) {
154 |             docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
155 |           }
156 |           if (docInfo != null) {
157 |             ObjectType lhsType =
158 |                 dereferenceToObject(n.getFirstChild().getJSType());
159 |             if (lhsType != null) {
160 |               // Put the JSDoc in the property slot, if there is one.
161 |               String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
162 |               if (lhsType.hasOwnProperty(propName)) {
163 |                 lhsType.setPropertyJSDocInfo(propName, docInfo, inExterns);
164 |               }
165 | 
166 |               // Put the JSDoc in any constructors or function shapes as well.
167 |               ObjectType propType =
168 |                   dereferenceToObject(lhsType.getPropertyType(propName));
169 |               if (propType != null) {
170 |                 attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(
171 |                     propType, docInfo, n.getQualifiedName());
172 |               }
173 |             }
174 |           }
175 |         }
176 |         break;
177 |     }
178 |   }
